questions.p: Nucleated settlement pattern na where houses dey pack together for one central point like market, well or junction, mostly for security and easy interaction. E different from scatter (dispersed) or straight-line (linear) pattern.

questions.q: In some farming communities, families live far apart from one another, each household close to its own farmland, with no central cluster of houses. This type of settlement pattern is called:
questions.e: When houses are scattered far apart, each close to the farmland it serves, this is called a dispersed (or scattered) settlement pattern. It is common in areas where farmers need to live close to their individual plots rather than grouping together.
questions.p: When houses dey spread far from each other, each house close to the farm wey e dey use, dem dey call am dispersed (scatter) settlement pattern. E common for places wey farmer need stay near im own farmland.

questions.q: Settlements that grow up in a straight or elongated form along a road, railway line, or river bank, such that the houses follow the course of the road or river, display a ___ settlement pattern.
questions.e: A linear settlement pattern occurs when houses are built in a line following a route such as a road, railway, or river, because the route provides easy access to transport, water, or trade. This gives the settlement an elongated shape rather than a compact or scattered one.
questions.p: Linear settlement pattern na when houses dey follow line along road, railway or river, because the route dey give better access to transport, water or trade. E go make the settlement get long shape instead of round or scatter shape.

questions.q: In Geography, which statement correctly describes the term 'site' of a settlement, as distinct from its 'situation'?
o: It is the relative position of a settlement compared to other settlements, roads, and resources around it
It is the actual physical ground or spot on which a settlement is built, including local features like a hill, river bank, or valley
It refers only to the total population living in the settlement
It refers to the official administrative boundary drawn around the settlement
questions.e: The 'site' of a settlement is the exact physical spot of land it occupies, such as a hilltop, river bank, or valley floor, which affected why it was first built there. 'Situation', on the other hand, describes its position relative to other places, roads, and resources, so the two terms must not be confused.
questions.p: 'Site' of settlement na the exact ground wey dem build am on top, like hilltop, river bank or valley, wey influence why dem first build there. 'Situation' na im position relative to other place and road, so no mix the two terms.

questions.q: According to central place theory, some towns act as 'central places' offering a wider range of higher-order goods and services (like specialist hospitals or universities) than surrounding smaller towns. The main reason for this is that such central places usually have:
o: An earlier founding date than all surrounding towns
Larger market areas (hinterlands) with more people able to support higher-order functions
A location on the coast, which is compulsory for every central place
Volcanic soil that makes farming more productive there
questions.e: Central place theory explains that bigger towns serve larger hinterlands (surrounding areas) with more customers, which is enough to support expensive, specialised services like universities or big hospitals. Smaller towns with fewer customers can only support everyday, lower-order services like small shops.
questions.p: Central place theory talk say big towns dey serve bigger area (hinterland) wey get plenty customer, and dat one go support costly special service like university or big hospital. Small towns wey no get plenty customer go just support small everyday service like small shop.

questions.q: Which of the following best distinguishes an urban settlement from a rural settlement?
o: An urban settlement is always located directly beside a river
An urban settlement has a small population mainly engaged in farming
An urban settlement has no schools, hospitals, or other social amenities
An urban settlement has a relatively large population mainly engaged in non-agricultural activities such as trade, administration, and industry
questions.e: Urban settlements (towns and cities) typically have large populations whose main work is non-farming activities like trade, government jobs, and industry, along with many social amenities. Rural settlements, by contrast, are smaller and mainly depend on farming.
questions.p: Urban settlement (towns and cities) dey get plenty people wey dey do non-farming work like trade, government job and industry, plus plenty social amenities. Rural settlement na small one wey mainly dey depend on farming.

questions.q: What is the main reason farmers practice crop rotation on their farmland?
o: To reduce the amount of rainfall received
To increase the size of the farm
To maintain and restore soil fertility
To increase the cost of labour needed
questions.e: Crop rotation involves growing different crops in sequence on the same land. This helps restore nutrients used up by previous crops and prevents soil exhaustion.
questions.p: Crop rotation na when farmer dey plant different crops for same land one after another. E dey help return nutrients wey old crop don use finish, so e dey keep the soil strong.

questions.q: Which solid mineral is mined in commercial quantity on the Jos Plateau in Nigeria?
questions.e: The Jos Plateau in Plateau State is well known as the major area for tin mining in Nigeria, dating back to colonial times.
questions.p: Jos Plateau for Plateau State na the main place wey dem dey mine tin for Nigeria, since colonial time.

questions.q: In shifting cultivation, farmers usually abandon a piece of land after some years mainly because of
o: decline in the fertility of the soil
sudden increase in the local population
too much rainfall on the land
questions.e: Shifting cultivation involves farming a plot until the soil nutrients are used up. Once yields fall due to reduced fertility, farmers move to a new plot and leave the old one to fallow.
questions.p: Shifting cultivation na when farmer dey use land until the soil nutrients don finish. Once yield begin reduce because soil no gree fertile again, farmer go move go another land make the old one rest.

questions.q: Manufacturing industries that take raw materials and process them into finished goods used directly by households, such as bread, shoes or soap, are known as
questions.e: Consumer goods industries produce finished products meant for direct use by the final consumer, unlike basic industries that produce materials used by other industries.
questions.p: Consumer goods industries na the ones wey dey produce finish products wey person go direct use, like bread or soap. Basic industries na different thing, dem dey produce material wey other industries go still use.

questions.q: When choosing a location for a large iron and steel industry, the most important factor is usually
o: nearness to a big market for finished goods
nearness to raw materials such as iron ore and coal
nearness to the coastline for tourism
availability of cheap unskilled labour alone
questions.e: Iron and steel production uses bulky, heavy raw materials like iron ore and coal. Transporting these long distances is costly, so such industries are usually sited close to the raw material sources to save cost.
questions.p: Iron and steel industry dey use heavy raw material like iron ore and coal. To carry dis kind heavy material go far go cost plenty money, so dem dey build the factory near where dem dey get the raw material.

questions.q: A cocoa farmer in Ondo State harvested 2400 kg of cocoa beans from his 3-hectare farm in one season. He sold all the beans at ₦1500 per kg, but spent ₦60000 on transporting the beans to the market. Calculate his net income from the sale.
questions.e: Total sales = 2400 kg x ₦1500 = ₦3,600,000. Net income = total sales minus transport cost = ₦3,600,000 - ₦60,000 = ₦3,540,000.
questions.p: Total money wey e sell = 2400 kg x ₦1500 = ₦3,600,000. Net income na when you minus the transport cost: ₦3,600,000 - ₦60,000 = ₦3,540,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why most manufacturing industries in Nigeria are concentrated in Lagos rather than in the mineral-rich areas of the Middle Belt?
o: Lagos has larger deposits of solid minerals than the Middle Belt
Lagos has port facilities, a large market and well-developed infrastructure
Lagos has more fertile agricultural land than the Middle Belt
The Middle Belt has no skilled workers at all
questions.e: Industrial location depends on more than raw materials; it also needs good transport, access to markets, power and skilled labour. Lagos, as a port city with a huge population and strong infrastructure, offers these advantages, so it attracts industries even though it is not a mining area.
questions.p: To site industry no be only raw material matter; good road, market, light and workers dey important too. Lagos na port city with plenty people and better infrastructure, so industries dey prefer am pass mining area for Middle Belt.

questions.q: Which type of agricultural practice is best described as the rearing of animals, such as cattle, over large open grasslands with little or no cultivation of crops?
questions.e: Pastoral farming focuses mainly on raising livestock, often over wide grassland areas, with little or no crop cultivation. This is common among herders such as the Fulani in the Nigerian savanna.
questions.p: Pastoral farming na when person focus on rearing animal like cow for wide grassland, without plant crop. Na dis kind farming Fulani herders dey do for Nigeria savanna area.

questions.q: Which mode of transport is generally the cheapest for moving bulky goods such as crude oil or grains over very long distances, provided a suitable route exists?
questions.e: Water transport (sea and inland waterways) can carry very large loads at once with low fuel cost per tonne, making it the cheapest for bulky goods over long distances. Road and air transport cost more per tonne for the same load.
questions.p: Water transport na the cheapest way to carry plenty heavy load for far distance because one ship fit carry plenty tonnes at once. Road and air cost more money for the same load.

questions.q: Trade that takes place between two or more different countries is best described as?
questions.e: International trade is trade carried out between different countries, involving exchange of goods and services across national borders. Local trade happens within one country or community.
questions.p: International trade na when two or more kontri dey exchange goods and services among demsef. Local trade na inside one kontri or community.

questions.q: Which of the following is the major factor that has limited the extensive development of railway networks in most West African countries?
o: High cost of construction and maintenance
Excessive rainfall throughout the entire year
Total absence of mineral resources to transport
Uniform flat relief across the whole region
questions.e: Building and maintaining railway lines requires huge capital for tracks, bridges, tunnels and rolling stock, which most West African governments find difficult to afford widely. The other options are not generally true for the whole region.
questions.p: To build and maintain railway need plenty money for rail, bridge and train wagon, and many West African kontri no get enough money for this. The other reasons no dey true for whole region.

questions.q: A country imports goods from one nation and, without processing them, re-exports the same goods to another country. This type of trade is called?
questions.e: Entrepot trade occurs when a country acts as a middleman, importing goods and re-exporting them unchanged to earn profit, often using its good port facilities. Singapore is a classic example of this type of trade.
questions.p: Entrepot trade na when one kontri just dey import goods come dey comot am again to another kontri without changing am, dem just dey use their good port to make profit. Singapore na good example.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa bought 50 bags of rice at ₦18,000 per bag in Lagos. He spent ₦2,500 per bag to transport all the bags to Maiduguri. He later sold each bag at ₦24,000 in Maiduguri. What was his total profit on all 50 bags?
questions.e: Total cost per bag = 18000 + 2500 = 20500. Profit per bag = 24000 - 20500 = 3500. Total profit for 50 bags = 3500 x 50 = 175000.
questions.p: Total cost for one bag na 18000 + 2500 = 20500. Profit for one bag na 24000 - 20500 = 3500. If you multiply 3500 by 50 bags, you go get 175000 total profit.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a true advantage of railway transport over road transport for moving goods?
o: Lower cost per tonne for bulk haulage over long distances
Door-to-door delivery directly to a customer's house without reloading
Less affected by traffic congestion on highways
Ability to move very heavy and bulky loads at once
questions.e: Railway transport is fixed to its tracks and stations, so goods usually need to be reloaded onto trucks for final delivery to a house, unlike road transport which can go door-to-door. The other three are real advantages of rail over road.
questions.p: Train dey follow only rail line and station, so dem must still carry the goods go another vehicle before e reach person house, unlike road wey fit go straight door-to-door. The other three options na correct advantage of rail pass road.

questions.q: Which major West African river serves as an important inland waterway linking Nigeria with countries such as Niger and Mali for the movement of goods and passengers?
questions.e: The River Niger is one of the longest rivers in West Africa and flows through several countries including Mali, Niger and Nigeria, making it an important route for inland water transport and trade. The other rivers listed are mainly local to Nigeria.
questions.p: River Niger na one of the longest river for West Africa, e dey pass through Mali, Niger and Nigeria, so e dey help for water transport and trade among dis kontris. The other rivers dey mostly inside Nigeria only.

questions.q: A delivery truck travels from Town A to Town B, a distance of 240 km, at a speed of 60 km/h. It returns from Town B to Town A along the same route at a speed of 40 km/h. What was the truck's average speed for the whole round trip?
questions.e: Time going = 240/60 = 4 hours. Time returning = 240/40 = 6 hours. Total distance = 480 km, total time = 10 hours, so average speed = 480/10 = 48 km/h.
questions.p: Time wey e take go na 240/60 = 4 hours, time wey e take return na 240/40 = 6 hours. Total distance na 480 km and total time na 10 hours, so average speed na 480/10 = 48 km/h.

questions.q: Nigeria is located approximately between which lines of latitude and longitude?
questions.e: Nigeria lies in West Africa, north of the Equator and east of the Greenwich Meridian. Its location is commonly given as about 4°N to 14°N and 3°E to 15°E.
questions.p: Nigeria dey West Africa, e dey north of Equator and east of Greenwich line. Dem dey always show am as 4°N to 14°N and 3°E to 15°E.

questions.q: Which of the following countries shares a common land border with Nigeria?
questions.e: Nigeria's neighbours are Benin (west), Niger (north), Chad (north-east, around Lake Chad) and Cameroon (east). Ghana, Senegal and Mali do not touch Nigeria's border.
questions.p: Nigeria neighbours na Benin, Niger, Chad (near Lake Chad) and Cameroon. Ghana, Senegal and Mali no dey border Nigeria at all.

questions.q: Which plateau contains Chappal Waddi, the highest point in Nigeria?
questions.e: Chappal Waddi, Nigeria's highest peak, is found on the Mambilla Plateau in Taraba State. Jos, Obudu and Biu are other plateaus but are not the location of this peak.
questions.p: Chappal Waddi, wey be di highest point for Nigeria, dey for Mambilla Plateau for Taraba State. Jos, Obudu and Biu na other plateau wey no be di correct answer.

questions.q: At which Nigerian town do River Niger and River Benue meet to form the famous Y-shaped confluence?
questions.e: River Niger and River Benue meet at Lokoja in Kogi State, forming a Y-shaped confluence. This is a well-known landmark in Nigerian geography.
questions.p: River Niger and River Benue dey meet for Lokoja, Kogi State, and dem form Y-shape confluence. Na popular landmark for Nigeria geography.

questions.q: Which climate type, according to the Koppen classification, best describes most of Nigeria's climate, with its distinct wet and dry seasons?
questions.e: Most of Nigeria experiences a tropical wet-and-dry (savanna) climate, classified as Aw, with a clear rainy season and dry season. Only the far south-east has true rainforest climate and only the far north edges into semi-arid conditions.
questions.p: Most part of Nigeria get tropical savanna climate (Aw) wey get clear rainy season and dry season. Na only small south-east get real rainforest climate, and small north part near semi-arid.

questions.q: The amount of annual rainfall in Nigeria generally decreases from the coast in the south towards the far north. What is the MAIN reason for this pattern?
o: The south receives rainfall only from the Harmattan wind
Moisture-laden winds from the Atlantic Ocean lose moisture as they move further inland and northward
The south has more rivers than the north
The north has more mountains that block rainfall
questions.e: Rain-bearing south-west winds from the Atlantic Ocean carry moisture that is progressively lost as the winds travel inland, so places far from the coast (like the north) get less rainfall. This, combined with the shorter stay of the moist air mass in the north, explains the decrease.
questions.p: Di rain-wind wey carry moisture from Atlantic Ocean dey lose im moisture as e dey travel go inland. So place wey far from sea, like north, dey get less rain pass south wey near sea.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the northern parts of Nigeria experience a longer dry season than the southern parts?
o: The north is farther from the moderating influence of the sea and is more affected by the dry continental Harmattan wind for a longer period
The north has more rainforest vegetation to retain moisture
The north is closer to the equator
The north has higher rainfall throughout the year
questions.e: The north is far inland, away from the sea, so the moist south-west monsoon winds reach it late and leave early, while the dry, dusty Harmattan wind from the Sahara blows over it for a longer time. This gives the north a longer dry season than the south.
questions.p: North dey far from sea, so di wet wind from south-west no dey reach dia quick and e dey leave early, while di dry Harmattan wind from Sahara dey blow for long time. Dat na why north dry season dey longer pass south own.

questions.q: In Northern Nigeria, the extensive savanna grassland with a long dry season and relatively low rainfall favours the large-scale cultivation of which staple food crop?
questions.e: Guinea corn (sorghum) is a drought-resistant cereal that grows well in the savanna climate of Northern Nigeria, which has low rainfall and a long dry season. Cocoa, oil palm and rubber need heavy rainfall and are grown in the forest belt of the south.
questions.p: Guinea corn fit survive for place wey rain no plenty and dry season long, like Northern Nigeria savanna. Cocoa, oil palm and rubber need plenty rain, na why dem dey grow for south forest area.

questions.q: Which of the following minerals is NOT regarded as a major mineral resource exploited in Nigeria?
questions.e: Nigeria has well-known deposits of coal (Enugu), tin (Jos Plateau) and petroleum (Niger Delta) that have been commercially exploited. Diamond is not a significant mineral resource found or mined in Nigeria.
questions.p: Nigeria get plenty coal for Enugu, tin for Jos Plateau and petroleum for Niger Delta wey dem dey mine well well. Diamond no be one of the major minerals wey dey Nigeria.

questions.q: The uneven distribution of population in Nigeria, with dense settlement in areas like the South-East and parts of the South-West and sparse settlement in parts of the Middle Belt, is mainly influenced by which factor?
o: Number of state capitals in each region
questions.e: Climate and soil fertility strongly affect how many people a land area can support through farming and settlement. Areas with good rainfall and fertile soils tend to attract denser population, while areas with poorer soils or tsetse fly infestation (common in parts of the Middle Belt) have sparser population. The other options do not directly explain population distribution patterns.
questions.p: Climate and good soil na wetin dey make land fit carry plenty people, because e go support farming well. Where rain good and soil fertile, people go gather pass; where soil no good or tsetse fly dey worry animals, population go low. The other options no really explain population spread.

questions.q: Large-scale coal mining in Nigeria, which once supplied fuel for the Nigerian Railway Corporation, is most closely associated with which town?
questions.e: Enugu is historically known as the centre of coal mining in Nigeria, with deposits that were mined for railway and industrial use. Jos is known for tin, Kano for groundnuts and trade, and Warri for petroleum activities.
questions.p: Enugu na the main place wey dem dey mine coal for Nigeria, and e be the fuel wey Railway Corporation use before. Jos na tin dem sabi am for, Kano na groundnut and trade, Warri na petroleum area.

questions.q: Most of Nigeria's major oil refineries and petrochemical industries are located in the Niger Delta region mainly because of which locational factor?
o: High altitude suitable for cooling plants
Availability of large tin ore deposits
Proximity to the source of crude oil
questions.e: Industries that process raw materials, such as oil refineries, are usually sited close to the source of the raw material to reduce transport costs. Since crude oil is extracted mainly in the Niger Delta, refineries are built there. The other options are not relevant locational factors for oil refining.
questions.p: Industry wey dey process raw material like crude oil dey like to dey near where dem dey get the raw material so transport cost go reduce. Na why oil refineries dey Niger Delta, because na there crude oil dey come from. The other options no get anything to do with am.

questions.q: Cocoa cultivation in Nigeria is concentrated mainly in the South-Western states such as Ondo and Oyo rather than in the far North. Which reason best explains this pattern?
o: The South-West has heavy rainfall and forest vegetation suitable for cocoa trees
Cocoa trees need very low temperatures found only in the North
Tin and columbite deposits are found only in the South-West
Cocoa requires sandy desert soil found mainly in the South-West
questions.e: Cocoa trees need heavy, well-distributed rainfall and forest conditions with partial shade, which are found in the South-Western rainforest belt, not in the drier savanna North. The other options describe conditions that do not match the real climatic or soil requirements of cocoa.
questions.p: Cocoa tree need plenty rain wey well spread and forest condition wey get small shade, and na South-West get dat kind weather, no be North wey dry pass. The other options no match the real condition wey cocoa need.

questions.q: A Nigerian state has a total population of 3,600,000 people and a land area of 24,000 square kilometres. Calculate the population density of the state in persons per square kilometre.
questions.e: Population density is found by dividing total population by land area: 3,600,000 divided by 24,000 equals 150 persons per square kilometre. This shows how crowded the state is on average.
questions.p: To find population density, divide total population by land area: 3,600,000 divide by 24,000 e give 150 persons per square kilometre. Na so dem dey measure how crowded one place be.

questions.q: Which of the following is the major means of transporting crude oil from oil fields to export terminals in Nigeria?
questions.e: Crude oil and petroleum products are mostly moved through pipelines from oil fields to terminals and refineries. Pipelines are cheap, continuous and safe for liquids over long distances compared to road, rail or air.
questions.p: Dem dey use pipeline carry crude oil comot from oil field go terminal. E cheap, e dey run anytime, and e better pass road, train or airplane for liquid like oil.

questions.q: The busiest seaport in Nigeria, located in Lagos State, handling the largest volume of import and export trade, is the:
questions.e: Apapa Port in Lagos is Nigeria's busiest seaport because Lagos is the commercial nerve centre of the country, with the highest concentration of industries and population, so most goods pass through it.
questions.p: Apapa Port for Lagos na the port wey busy pass for Nigeria because Lagos na the main commercial centre, plenty industry and people dey there, so plenty goods dey pass there.

questions.q: In international trade, when the value of a country's imports exceeds the value of its exports over a given period, this situation is called:
questions.e: When imports (money spent abroad) are more than exports (money earned from abroad), the country has an unfavourable (or adverse) balance of trade. A favourable balance or surplus would mean exports exceed imports instead.
questions.p: If import (money wey dem spend abroad) pass export (money wey dem earn), na unfavourable balance of trade be dat. If export pass import, na favourable balance instead.

questions.q: Which of these factors best explains why road transport carries a much larger share of goods and passenger traffic within Nigeria than railway transport does?
o: Roads are generally cheaper to construct and maintain than railway tracks
The road network is more extensive and reaches remote rural areas that railway lines do not cover
Railway wagons have a smaller carrying capacity than trucks
Government policy deliberately favours road transport over railway transport
questions.e: Nigeria's road network spreads into almost every town and village, including remote rural farming areas, while railway lines are fixed to only a few routes connecting major cities. This flexibility and wider coverage make road transport dominant, not wagon size or cost alone.
questions.p: Road network dey reach almost every town and village for Nigeria, even remote village, but railway line only dey follow few routes between big cities. Na dis wide coverage and flexibility make road transport dey carry pass, no be only wagon size or cost.

questions.q: Nigeria's trade whereby goods are imported from one country and later re-exported to another country without being substantially used or processed locally is best described as:
questions.e: Entrepot trade happens when a country imports goods mainly to re-export them to a third country, often using its port facilities as a transit point, rather than consuming the goods itself.
questions.p: Entrepot trade na when country import goods just to re-export am go another country, dem dey use their port as transit point, no be say dem go use the goods for inside their own country.

questions.q: A major seasonal obstacle to the use of rivers such as the Niger and Benue for large-scale inland waterway transport in Nigeria is:
o: presence of numerous bridges that block the passage of vessels
the high cost of fuel needed to power the boats
excessive rainfall causing flooding of the river banks
low water levels during the dry season due to reduced river discharge
questions.e: During the dry season, rainfall reduces drastically, causing the volume and depth of rivers like the Niger and Benue to fall, which makes it difficult for large vessels to navigate safely. This seasonal shallowness, not flooding or bridges, is the key constraint on year-round water transport.
questions.p: For dry season, rain dey reduce well well, so river like Niger and Benue dey shallow and small, e no go gree big boat pass well. Na dis seasonal shallow water, no be flood or bridge, be the main problem for water transport throughout the year.

questions.q: ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) was formally established after the signing of a treaty in which year?
questions.e: ECOWAS was created in 1975 when the Treaty of Lagos was signed by West African leaders to promote economic cooperation and integration in the region.
questions.p: Na for 1975 dem sign di Treaty of Lagos wey bring ECOWAS come be. Dis treaty na im start di economic cooperation for West Africa.

questions.q: The permanent headquarters (secretariat) of ECOWAS is located in which city?
questions.e: The ECOWAS Commission's headquarters is in Abuja, the capital of Nigeria, which also reflects Nigeria's leading role in founding and funding the organisation.
questions.p: ECOWAS headquarters dey Abuja, Nigeria. Nigeria na one of di major founder and sponsor of ECOWAS.

questions.q: How many West African countries originally signed the Treaty of Lagos in 1975 to form ECOWAS?
questions.e: Fifteen West African countries, including Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal and others, signed the Treaty of Lagos in 1975 to establish ECOWAS as a regional economic bloc.
questions.p: Fifteen (15) kontri for West Africa, like Nigeria, Ghana and Senegal, sign di Treaty of Lagos for 1975 wey bring ECOWAS come.

questions.q: Which of the following West African countries has no direct access to the Atlantic Ocean, making it a landlocked country?
questions.e: Niger is surrounded entirely by other countries (Algeria, Libya, Chad, Nigeria, Benin, Burkina Faso and Mali) and has no coastline, unlike Ghana, Senegal and Sierra Leone which all border the Atlantic Ocean.
questions.p: Niger no get any coastline, e dey surrounded by other kontris like Nigeria, Chad, Mali and Algeria. Ghana, Senegal and Sierra Leone all get sea coast.

questions.q: A geography student wants to list a group of West African countries that are ALL landlocked (no coastline on the Atlantic Ocean or Gulf of Guinea). Which option below contains ONLY landlocked countries?
questions.e: Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso are the three landlocked countries in West Africa with no sea access. Ghana, Togo, Benin and Liberia all have coastlines along the Atlantic Ocean or Gulf of Guinea, so any option mixing them in is wrong.
questions.p: Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso no get sea for dia border at all, na dem be landlocked for West Africa. Ghana, Togo, Benin and Liberia all get coast, so any option wey mix dem no correct.

questions.q: Starting from the Nigerian coast and moving northward towards the Sahel region, rainfall decreases steadily. Which sequence correctly shows the natural vegetation belts in the order they appear from south (coast) to north?
o: Guinea savanna - Rainforest - Mangrove forest - Sudan savanna - Sahel savanna
Mangrove forest - Rainforest - Guinea savanna - Sudan savanna - Sahel savanna
Rainforest - Mangrove forest - Sahel savanna - Sudan savanna - Guinea savanna
Sahel savanna - Sudan savanna - Guinea savanna - Rainforest - Mangrove forest
questions.e: As rainfall decreases from the coast to the far north, vegetation changes from mangrove swamp forest along the coast, to rainforest, then guinea savanna, sudan savanna and finally sahel savanna near the desert edge. This order matches the actual rainfall gradient across Nigeria and West Africa.
questions.p: As rain dey reduce from coast go north, di vegetation dey change from mangrove for coast, go rainforest, den guinea savanna, sudan savanna, finish with sahel savanna near desert side. Na dis order follow di rainfall pattern well well.

questions.q: Because of different colonial histories, ECOWAS member states mainly use three official languages for government business. Which of these languages is NOT one of the main official languages used across ECOWAS countries?
questions.e: West African countries were colonised mainly by Britain, France and Portugal, so English, French and Portuguese remain the main official languages used in ECOWAS states. Spanish was not a major colonial language in West Africa.
questions.p: West Africa get British, French and Portuguese colonial masters, so English, French and Portuguese na di main official languages. Spanish no be major colonial language for West Africa at all.

questions.q: A map covers a rectangular area of 10 km by 8 km on the ground. If the scale of the map is 1:200000, what will be the area of this region on the map, in square centimetres?
questions.e: At a scale of 1:200000, 1 cm on the map represents 2 km on the ground, so 10 km becomes 5 cm and 8 km becomes 4 cm on the map. Multiplying these map lengths gives 5 cm x 4 cm = 20 square centimetres.
questions.p: With 1:200000 scale, 1 cm na 2 km for ground, so 10 km turn 5 cm and 8 km turn 4 cm. When you multiply 5 cm and 4 cm, you get 20 square centimetres.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a representative fraction (RF) as used in map reading?
o: A ratio, with no units attached, showing one unit of map distance to the equivalent number of the same unit on the ground
A line drawn on a map and divided into equal parts to show distance
A written statement such as 1 centimetre represents 1 kilometre
A ratio showing map distance to ground distance measured in different units
questions.e: A representative fraction is a unitless ratio, for example 1:50000, meaning one unit on the map equals 50000 of the same unit on the ground. This allows the scale to be used with any unit of measurement, unlike a statement scale.
questions.p: Representative fraction no get unit at all, e mean say one unit for map na the exact same unit for ground. Like 1:50000, e dey show say one unit for map na 50000 of that same unit for ground.

questions.q: A straight road on a map is measured with a piece of thread, which is then straightened and found to be 9 cm long. If the map's scale is 1:150000, what is the actual length of the road in kilometres?
questions.e: At a scale of 1:150000, 1 cm on the map equals 150000 cm, which is 1.5 km, on the ground. Multiplying the measured 9 cm by 1.5 km gives 13.5 kilometres.
questions.p: As the scale be 1:150000, 1 cm for map na 1.5 km for ground. When you multiply that 9 cm by 1.5 km, you go get 13.5 kilometres.

questions.q: A surveyor wants to enlarge a map whose scale is 1:40000 so that the new scale becomes 1:10000. By what factor must the linear dimensions of features on the original map be multiplied to produce the new map?
questions.e: Enlarging from 1:40000 to 1:10000 means each unit on the new map represents a smaller ground distance, so the map becomes more detailed and larger. The enlargement factor is found by dividing 40000 by 10000, which gives 4 times.
questions.p: To change scale from 1:40000 go 1:10000, you must make the map bigger. If you divide 40000 by 10000, you go get 4 times as the enlargement factor.

questions.q: On a topographical map, the distance between two boreholes is shown as 6 cm. The statement scale given on the map reads '1 centimetre represents 2 kilometres'. What is the actual ground distance between the boreholes?
questions.e: The statement scale tells us directly that every 1 cm on the map equals 2 km on the ground. Multiplying the measured 6 cm by 2 km per cm gives 12 kilometres.
questions.p: The statement scale talk say 1 cm na 2 km for ground. So if you multiply 6 cm by 2 km, you go get 12 kilometres for ground distance.

questions.q: A footpath on a map follows a winding course and is measured along its curves using a divider set to small equal steps, giving a total of 11 cm. If the map scale is 1:25000, what is the approximate actual length of the footpath, in metres?
questions.e: At a scale of 1:25000, 1 cm on the map represents 25000 cm, which is 250 metres, on the ground. Multiplying the measured 11 cm by 250 metres gives 2750 metres.
questions.p: For 1:25000 scale, 1 cm na 250 metres for ground. When you multiply 11 cm by 250 metres, you go get 2750 metres.

questions.q: Two towns, Giwa and Rimi, appear on separate maps drawn at different scales. On Map X, drawn at 1:20000, the towns are 15 cm apart. On Map Y, drawn at 1:60000, what distance in centimetres would represent the same real ground distance between the two towns?
questions.e: The real ground distance is first found using Map X: 15 cm multiplied by 20000 gives 300000 cm, which is 3 km. On Map Y, since 1 cm represents 60000 cm, dividing 300000 cm by 60000 gives 5 centimetres representing the same distance.
questions.p: First find the real ground distance for Map X as 300000 cm. When you use Map Y scale to divide am, you go get 5 centimetres.

questions.q: On a topographical map, closely spaced contour lines represent a steep slope while widely spaced contour lines represent a gentle slope. This relationship exists mainly because:
o: Contour spacing depends only on the colour used by the map maker
Closely spaced contours indicate that the area has a low population density
Closely spaced contours indicate a rapid change in height over a short horizontal distance
Widely spaced contours always indicate the presence of a river valley
questions.e: Contour spacing shows how fast height changes with distance. When contours are close together, a large height change occurs over a short distance, giving a steep gradient; when far apart, the height change is gradual, giving a gentle gradient.
questions.p: Contour spacing dey show how height dey change with distance. When contours close, big height change dey happen for short distance, wey dey give steep gradient.

questions.q: A hiker walks from a point on a map marked 400 m above sea level to another point marked 250 m above sea level. The horizontal distance between the two points, measured on a map of scale 1:25,000, is 6 cm. What is the gradient of the slope between the two points? (Give your answer as a ratio 1:n)
questions.e: Vertical interval = 400 - 250 = 150 m. Horizontal equivalent = 6 cm x 25,000 = 150,000 cm = 1500 m. Gradient = 150:1500 = 1:10.
questions.p: Vertical interval na 400 - 250 = 150 m. Horizontal equivalent na 6 cm x 25,000 = 1500 m, so gradient na 150:1500 wey come be 1:10.

questions.q: A surveyor wants to construct a cross-section (relief profile) along a straight line drawn between two towns on a topographical map. Which of the following is the FIRST correct step in constructing the profile?
o: Place the straight edge of a plain paper along the section line and mark where each contour crosses it
Measure the bearing of one town from the other
Calculate the gradient between the two towns
Colour the map according to height ranges
questions.e: To draw a cross-section, the first practical step is to lay a strip of paper along the chosen line on the map and transfer the points where contours cross it, before plotting these heights on a graph. Gradient and bearing calculations come later or are unrelated.
questions.p: To draw cross-section, first thing na to put plain paper along the line and mark where contours cross am. Na after you go plot am on graph.

questions.q: On a cross-section drawn from a topographical map, a vertical scale of 1 cm to represent 50 m and a horizontal scale of 1 cm to represent 500 m were used. This means the vertical scale has been exaggerated by a factor of:
questions.e: Vertical exaggeration equals the horizontal scale value divided by the vertical scale value, both converted to the same units. Since 1 cm represents 500 m horizontally but only 50 m vertically, the vertical scale is exaggerated 500/50 = 10 times.
questions.p: Vertical exaggeration na horizontal scale divide by vertical scale. Since 500 divide by 50 na 10, the vertical scale exaggerate by 10 times.

questions.q: On a topographical map, a flat-topped hill with very steep sides is shown by contour lines that are:
o: Widely spaced near the base and very close together near a flat summit area where they stop appearing
Evenly spaced from the base to the summit
Arranged in a perfectly straight line across the map
Very close together near the base and widely spaced near a flat summit area where they stop appearing
questions.e: A flat-topped hill with steep sides has contours tightly packed near the base, showing a rapid rise, and then no further contours over the flat summit since the land levels off there. This pattern is typical of a plateau-like hill or mesa.
questions.p: Flat-topped hill with steep sides get contours wey tight near base to show sharp rise. When e reach flat summit, contours go stop to show say ground level down.

questions.q: On a topographical map, contour lines that form a set of closed loops decreasing in value towards the centre, with the innermost loop lower than all others, most likely represent a:
questions.e: When contour values decrease inward instead of increasing, the land surface is sinking towards the centre, which shows a depression or basin rather than a hill.
questions.p: If contour line value dey reduce as e dey go inside, e mean say di ground dey sink. Na so we take sabi say na depression or basin, no bi hill.

questions.q: A valley on a topographical map is best recognised by contour lines that:
o: Bend to form V-shapes pointing downhill away from the stream
Form perfect circles of increasing value outward
Bend to form V-shapes pointing uphill, often with a stream in the V
Run as straight parallel lines evenly spaced apart
questions.e: In a valley, contour lines are pushed upstream by the river cutting into the land, so the V points towards higher ground (upstream), unlike a ridge where the V points downhill.
questions.p: For valley, contour line dey bend like V wey point go uphill. Na di river wey dey cut di land dey cause dis shape.

questions.q: On a map drawn to a scale of 1:25,000, the horizontal distance between two points, X and Y, measured on the map is 8 cm. If X lies on the 300 m contour and Y lies on the 450 m contour, what is the gradient of the slope from X to Y expressed as a ratio?
questions.e: Ground distance = 8 cm x 25,000 = 200,000 cm = 2000 m. Vertical rise = 450 - 300 = 150 m. Gradient = horizontal/vertical = 2000/150, which simplifies to about 1 in 13.3.
questions.p: Ground distance na 2000 m and vertical rise na 150 m. If you divide 2000 by 150, you go get 13.3, so di gradient na 1 in 13.3.

questions.q: In constructing a relief profile (cross-section) along a line on a topographical map, a candidate first transfers the points where the line crosses each contour onto the edge of a strip of paper. The next correct step is to:
o: Measure the straight-line distance between the two end towns using a ruler
Plot each transferred point against its contour height on graph paper using a chosen vertical scale, then join the points
Shade the area under the highest contour value only
Draw concentric circles around each contour crossing point
questions.e: After marking where the line crosses each contour on the paper strip, the next step is to transfer these points to graph paper, plot each against its height using the vertical scale, and join them smoothly to form the profile.
questions.p: After you mark di contour points for paper, you go transfer dem go graph paper. You go plot dem based on dia height and join dem to see di shape.

questions.q: A cross-section is drawn using a horizontal scale of 1:50,000 and a vertical scale of 1 cm to represent 100 m. What is the vertical exaggeration (VE) of this cross-section?
questions.e: Horizontal scale 1:50,000 means 1 cm represents 50,000 cm = 500 m horizontally. Vertical exaggeration = horizontal metres per cm divided by vertical metres per cm = 500/100 = 5.
questions.p: Horizontal scale mean say 1 cm na 500 m. If you divide 500 m by 100 m, you go get 5 as di vertical exaggeration.

questions.q: A hiker at Ogbonna village observes a hilltop on a bearing of 118°. What is the bearing of Ogbonna village from the hilltop?
questions.e: Since 118° is less than 180°, the back bearing is found by adding 180°. 118° + 180° = 298°.
questions.p: Because 118° no reach 180°, you go add 180° to find the back bearing. If you add 118° plus 180°, e go give you 298°.

questions.q: A six-figure grid reference is written as 234 561. What does this grid reference represent on a topographical map?
o: A compass bearing expressed in grid units
The distance in kilometres from the map's origin to the point
A grid square bounded by eastings 23 and 24, and northings 56 and 57
A single point located using an easting of 234 and a northing of 561
questions.e: A six-figure grid reference gives a precise point by reading the easting (first three digits) and then the northing (last three digits), each subdivided into tenths of a grid square. This pinpoints an exact location rather than a whole square.
questions.p: Six-figure grid reference dey show correct single point by reading easting (first three numbers) and northing (last three numbers). E dey point exact location instead of just the whole square.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the difference between a 'true bearing' and a 'magnetic bearing' of a point?
o: True bearing is measured from true north while magnetic bearing is measured from the direction a compass needle points
True bearing is always greater than magnetic bearing by exactly 90°
True bearing applies only to distances less than 1 km while magnetic bearing applies to longer distances
True bearing is measured clockwise while magnetic bearing is measured anticlockwise
questions.e: True north is the direction to the geographic North Pole, whereas magnetic north is the direction a compass needle points, which can differ due to magnetic declination. Both bearings are measured clockwise, just from different reference norths.
questions.p: True north na the real geographic North Pole, but magnetic north na where compass needle dey point because of magnetic declination. Both of them dey measure clockwise, just say dem get different north reference.

questions.q: A cyclist travels from point X on a bearing of 300° to point Y. On reaching Y, in what general compass direction must he look to see point X, without calculating the exact bearing?
questions.e: A bearing of 300° from X points towards the north-west, so looking back from Y towards X means facing the opposite general direction, which is south-east.
questions.p: If bearing from X na 300°, e mean say you dey face north-west. When you wan look back from Y go X, you must face opposite direction, wey be south-east.

questions.q: On a compass rose, a hunter faces North and turns clockwise through three-quarters of a full revolution to face a new direction. Which cardinal direction is he now facing, and what bearing does this represent?
questions.e: A full revolution is 360°, so three-quarters of it is 270°. Turning clockwise from North by 270° brings the hunter to face West.
questions.p: Full circle na 360°, so three-quarter of am na 270°. If you turn clockwise from North by 270°, na West you go land.

questions.q: Two towns, Efon and Isua, are shown on a map. Efon lies at grid reference 10 20 and Isua lies at grid reference 10 35, with the northing values increasing towards the top of the map (north). What is the bearing of Isua from Efon?
questions.e: Both towns share the same easting (10), but Isua has a higher northing (35 compared to 20), meaning Isua lies directly north of Efon. A point due north has a bearing of 000°.
questions.p: Both towns dey use the same easting (10), but Isua northing high pass Efon, wey mean say Isua dey straight up north. Any place wey dey straight north get bearing of 000°.

questions.q: An examiner tells a candidate that a point R is located on a bearing of 225° from point S. Which of the following statements correctly describes the position of R relative to S?
questions.e: A bearing of 225° falls exactly between south (180°) and west (270°), which corresponds to the south-west direction. Candidates often confuse this with north-west by miscounting the quadrant.
questions.p: Bearing of 225° stay straight for middle of south (180°) and west (270°), wey be south-west. Make you no confuse am with north-west.

questions.q: A surveyor is carrying out a chain survey of a triangular farmland near Minna. To fix the exact position of a tree inside the triangle relative to the chain line, she measures the perpendicular distance from the tree to the chain line and the distance along the chain line to the foot of this perpendicular. This method of fixing a point is called
questions.e: Offsetting is the method of locating points by measuring a perpendicular distance (offset) from a point to the main chain line. It is the basic method used in chain surveying to plot details.
questions.p: Na offsetting dem dey call am when surveyor measure perpendicular distance from tree go join chain line to fix where the tree dey. Na base method be that for chain surveying to plot details.

questions.q: In a levelling exercise along a road under construction in Kaduna, a surveyor sets up a levelling instrument and takes a back sight reading of 2.150 m on a benchmark known to be 320.500 m above sea level. The foresight reading on the next point is 1.300 m. What is the reduced level of the next point?
questions.e: Height of instrument = 320.500 + 2.150 = 322.650 m. Reduced level of the next point = 322.650 - 1.300 = 321.350 m.
questions.p: To find am, you go first add back sight 2.150 m to benchmark 320.500 m to get height of instrument as 322.650 m. Then you minus foresight 1.300 m from am to get 321.350 m as the reduced level.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important reason why surveyors use triangulation when mapping a large area such as a state in Nigeria?
o: It removes the need for a baseline measurement
It eliminates the need for any angular measurement
It replaces the need for GIS software in mapping
It allows accurate control points to be fixed over long distances using a network of triangles
questions.e: Triangulation establishes a network of connected triangles with known angles and a measured baseline, allowing accurate positions of control points to be fixed over wide areas. This gives a reliable framework for detailed surveys.
questions.p: Triangulation dey use network of triangles with known angles and baseline to fix accurate control points over wide areas. E dey give reliable framework for big survey work.

questions.q: A GIS analyst in a Lagos State planning office wants to combine a layer showing flood-prone areas with a layer showing residential buildings, in order to identify houses at risk of flooding. Which key GIS operation is being applied here?
questions.e: Overlay analysis combines two or more spatial data layers to produce new information, such as identifying buildings that fall within flood-prone zones. This is a core analytical function of GIS.
questions.p: Na overlay analysis dem dey use combine two or more map layers together. E dey help show houses wey dey inside flood-prone zone for GIS.

questions.q: A survey team setting out the foundation of a new market in Bida uses a simple instrument made of two crossed arms fixed at right angles on a pole, with sighting slits, to set out perpendicular lines on the ground. This instrument is called a
questions.e: A cross staff is a simple surveying instrument with two perpendicular sighting lines used mainly to set out right angles in chain surveying. It is commonly used for locating offsets accurately.
questions.p: Cross staff na simple instrument wey get two crossed arms wey dem dey use set out right angles for ground. E dey help surveyor locate offsets well well.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the length of daylight varies between seasons at a place like Enugu, instead of being exactly 12 hours every day of the year?
o: The earth's distance from the moon changes with seasons
The earth's axis is tilted as it revolves around the sun
The earth spins faster during the day than at night
The earth rotates at different speeds throughout the year
questions.e: Because the earth's axis is tilted and stays pointed in the same direction as the earth orbits the sun, different parts of the earth receive varying hours of daylight at different times of the year. This tilt, not changes in rotation speed, causes the seasonal variation in day length.
questions.p: Na because the earth axis dey tilted as e dey go round the sun, naim make daylight length dey change for Enugu and other places. If not be this tilt, everywhere for earth for dey get 12 hours daylight everyday.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most accurate reason why the International Date Line is drawn mostly along the 180° meridian rather than a straight line through populated areas?
o: To ensure the line matches the Greenwich Meridian exactly
To make the line pass through the Equator for balance
To avoid splitting a single country or landmass into two different calendar dates
To reduce the number of time zones in the world
questions.e: The 180 degree meridian runs mostly through the Pacific Ocean, so the International Date Line is bent at certain points to avoid cutting through countries or island groups, which would otherwise force one part of a nation to be a day ahead of the other part.
questions.p: Dem draw the International Date Line make e bend for some places so say e no go cut any country into two different days. E dey follow 180° meridian mostly for inside Pacific Ocean to make life easy for people wey dey stay near.

questions.q: The layer of the earth found between the crust and the core, made up largely of dense silicate rocks containing magnesium and iron, is called the:
questions.e: The mantle lies directly below the crust and above the core, and it is composed mainly of iron and magnesium-rich silicate rocks. It is the thickest layer of the earth.
questions.p: Na mantle dey stay right under crust and above core, and e get iron and magnesium. E bi the thickest layer for earth.

questions.q: Chinwe observed a rock sample made up of visibly different mineral grains such as quartz, feldspar and mica, tightly interlocked without any layering or banding. This texture is most typical of rocks formed by the:
o: Rapid cooling of lava on the earth's surface
Recrystallisation of rocks under extreme pressure
Slow cooling of magma deep within the earth
questions.e: When magma cools slowly deep underground, large interlocking crystals of different minerals have time to form, as seen in coarse-grained igneous rocks like granite. Rapid cooling at the surface instead produces fine-grained rocks.
questions.p: If magma cool down slow for inside ground, big crystal go form like granite. Na so coarse-grained igneous rocks dey take form.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the general relationship between the earth's crust, mantle and core in terms of thickness and temperature?
o: The mantle is thinner than the crust but hotter than the core
The crust is the thinnest layer while temperature generally increases towards the core
The crust is the thickest layer and the core has the lowest temperature
The core is the thinnest layer but has the highest temperature
questions.e: The crust is a thin outer shell compared to the much thicker mantle and core, and temperature rises steadily from the crust down to the extremely hot core. This pattern is well established from seismic and geothermal studies.
questions.p: Crust na the thinest layer, and heat dey increase as you dey go down reach core. Temperature high gidigba for the center of earth.

questions.q: A sample of rock from a riverbed in Kogi State shows distinct layers (strata), contains fossils of ancient shells, and can be easily scratched with a knife. These features strongly suggest the rock is:
questions.e: Layering, fossils and softness are classic features of sedimentary rocks, which form from the gradual deposition and compaction of sediments, often in water. Igneous and metamorphic rocks do not typically show fossils or distinct bedding.
questions.p: Wetin get layers, fossils and soft to scratch na sedimentary rock. Dem dey form from particles wey join together for water.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why metamorphic rocks are generally harder and more compact than the original rocks from which they formed?
o: They are formed only from the direct cooling of molten magma
Intense heat and pressure cause recrystallisation of minerals into a denser arrangement
They contain large amounts of trapped water that hardens over time
They are formed from loose, newly deposited sediments only
questions.e: Metamorphism involves subjecting existing rocks to great heat and pressure without melting them completely, which causes minerals to recrystallise into tightly packed, denser structures. This is why metamorphic rocks like quartzite are harder than their parent rocks.
questions.p: Hotness and pressure dey make mineral recrystallise into tight arrangement. Na why metamorphic rock come hard pass the original one.

questions.q: A student wants to identify an unknown mineral sample found near a mining site in Plateau State. Which pair of properties would be most useful and reliable for this identification?
o: Weight of the sample and the time it took to form
Size of the sample and the name given to it by local miners
Hardness and crystal form of the mineral
Colour of the sample and the location where it was found
questions.e: Hardness and crystal form are consistent physical properties controlled by a mineral's internal atomic structure, making them reliable for identification. Colour can vary due to impurities, and size, location or local names are not scientific identification criteria.
questions.p: Hardness and crystal form na the best way to know mineral because dem dey follow atomic structure. Colour fit lie sometimes because of impurities.

questions.q: A block of land that is forced upward between two parallel normal faults, standing higher than the land on either side, is called a
questions.e: When the land between two faults is pushed up relative to the surrounding blocks, it forms a horst. A graben is the opposite, a sunken block between faults.
questions.p: When land block go up between two faults, we dey call am horst. If the land block come sink down, na graben be that.

questions.q: Which of the following is the BEST evidence that a rock mass has undergone faulting rather than folding?
o: The rock layers are tilted gently in one direction only
The rock layers are bent into wave-like curves without breaking
The rock layers show a visible crack with one side displaced relative to the other
The rock layers become more compact and denser without cracking
questions.e: Faulting involves a break (fracture) in rock strata followed by displacement of the blocks along the crack. Folding, by contrast, bends rock layers without breaking them.
questions.p: Faulting mean say rock break and move from im original position. Folding just dey bend rock like cloth without breaking am.

questions.q: A town built directly on a volcanic cone is most likely to experience fertile soils over time mainly because
o: lava flows cool the surrounding air and increase rainfall
the steep slopes of volcanoes prevent soil erosion
volcanic eruptions clear away existing poor soils completely
weathered volcanic ash and lava are rich in minerals that enrich the soil
questions.e: Volcanic materials such as ash and lava contain minerals like potassium and phosphorus which, after weathering, make surrounding soils very fertile. This is why many volcanic regions support rich agriculture.
questions.p: Volcano ash and lava get plenty minerals like potassium. When dem weather finish, dem dey make the soil very good for farming.

questions.q: The point on the Earth's surface directly above the origin of an earthquake, where shock waves are first felt and are usually most destructive, is known as the
questions.e: The focus is the actual point inside the Earth where the earthquake originates, while the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above it. The epicentre experiences the strongest shaking.
questions.p: Focus na the point inside ground where earthquake start. The epicentre na the point wey dey direct top of the focus for surface.

questions.q: A geography student observes a landscape where molten rock cooled slowly far below the surface and was later exposed after millions of years of erosion removed the overlying rock. This landform is best described as a product of
questions.e: Intrusive vulcanicity occurs when magma cools and solidifies beneath the Earth's surface, forming features like batholiths that are only exposed later after overlying rocks are eroded away. Extrusive vulcanicity instead involves magma reaching the surface directly.
questions.p: Intrusive vulcanicity happen when magma cool down inside ground. After long time, erosion go comot the top rock make the landform show.

questions.q: In a region undergoing tension (stretching) of the Earth's crust, two parallel faults develop and the central block slips downward relative to the blocks on either side. Over millions of years, this sunken valley may be occupied by a river or lake. This landform is called a
questions.e: A rift valley, also called a graben, forms when a central block of land drops down between two parallel faults due to tensional forces. The East African Rift Valley is a classic real-world example.
questions.p: When land block sink down between two parallel faults, we dey call am rift valley or graben. Na tension force dey cause this one.

questions.q: At a seismic monitoring station in Abuja, geologists recorded that an earthquake's secondary (S) waves arrived 8 minutes after the primary (P) waves. If the time difference increases by 1 minute for roughly every 125 km of distance from the epicentre to the station, how far was the station from the epicentre?
questions.e: Multiply the time difference by the distance covered per minute: 8 minutes multiplied by 125 km gives 1000 km. This method uses the known lag between P and S wave arrival times to estimate distance to the epicentre.
questions.p: If 1 minute equal 125 km, then 8 minutes go be 8 times 125. That one give us 1000 km as the distance.

questions.q: Which of these best explains why earthquakes and volcanic eruptions are commonly found along the same narrow belts on the Earth's surface, such as the Pacific Ring of Fire?
o: Both are caused by heavy rainfall weakening the crust in those belts
Both occur mainly where ocean currents are strongest
Both result from the movement and interaction of tectonic plates at their boundaries
Both are caused by human activities such as mining and construction
questions.e: Tectonic plate boundaries are zones of intense crustal stress where plates collide, separate, or slide past one another, triggering both earthquakes and volcanic activity. This explains why these two phenomena cluster along the same belts like the Pacific Ring of Fire.
questions.p: Earthquake and volcano dey happen for same place because of tectonic plate movement. Where plates dey meet or pull apart, stress dey high.

questions.q: Onyeka observed that a layer of iron-rich rock in his village near Itakpe had turned reddish-brown and become crumbly after many years of exposure to air and moisture, without any change in its mineral arrangement by plant or animal action. Which chemical weathering process is responsible for this change?
questions.e: Oxidation occurs when iron-bearing minerals react with oxygen in the presence of moisture, forming reddish-brown iron oxides and weakening the rock. Exfoliation is a physical process, while carbonation and hydrolysis involve different chemical reactions.
questions.p: Na oxidation dey happen when iron for rock come meet oxygen plus water, con turn am red-brown and weak. Dem other options no be chemical weathering like dis one.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why biological weathering is generally more active in a tropical rainforest region of Nigeria than in the semi-arid far north?
o: Frequent sandstorms expose fresh rock surfaces in the forest
Lower temperatures in the forest cause more frost action
Higher wind speeds in the forest increase rock abrasion
Dense vegetation and abundant soil organisms thrive in the warm, humid conditions, increasing root action and organic acid production
questions.e: Warm, humid conditions in the rainforest support dense plant growth and many soil organisms, whose roots and decaying matter release organic acids that break down rocks. The semi-arid north lacks this vegetation density, so biological weathering is weaker there.
questions.p: Hot and wet weather for rainforest dey make plant and small-small organism plenty well-well. Dem roots and acid wey dem dey drop dey quickly scatter rocks pass as e be for dry north.

questions.q: A geography student studying a hillside in Mambilla Plateau noticed a series of small, step-like terraces on a grassy slope, each terrace held up by a tiny ridge of soil, with no visible break or sudden collapse. This landform most likely results from which type of mass movement?
questions.e: Soil creep is an extremely slow downslope movement that often produces small terracettes (step-like ridges) on grassy slopes over a long time. Landslides and mudflows are sudden and rapid, while rock fall involves falling rock fragments, not terraced soil.
questions.p: Na soil creep dey cause those small-small steps wey dem dey see for grass slope as soil dey small-small waka go down. Landslide and mudflow dey happen quick-quick, no be like dis one.

questions.q: Which of the following factors would most directly reduce the rate of mass movement on a slope, assuming all other conditions remain the same?
o: Continuous heavy rainfall soaking the soil
Removal of vegetation cover by bush burning
Planting of deep-rooted trees and grasses on the slope
Increase in slope angle due to road construction
questions.e: Deep-rooted plants bind soil particles together and absorb excess water, which increases slope stability and reduces mass movement. The other options either remove support or add weight and lubrication, encouraging movement.
questions.p: If you plant trees with deep roots for slope, dem go hold the soil tight-tight and drink water so the land no go scatter. Dem other actions go make the soil fall down quick.

questions.q: A block of limestone and a block of granite of similar size were left exposed to the same rainy tropical climate for fifty years. Which observation would best confirm that chemical weathering acted more intensely on the limestone than on the granite?
o: The limestone block became smaller and pitted with hollows, while the granite showed little change
Both blocks increased in size due to mineral deposition
The granite block disappeared completely while the limestone remained solid
Both blocks cracked only along straight lines due to temperature changes
questions.e: Limestone is composed mainly of calcium carbonate, which dissolves readily in rainwater containing carbonic acid, producing pitted, reduced rock surfaces. Granite is more resistant to this carbonation process, so it would show far less chemical decay under the same conditions.
questions.p: Water and acid dey easily scatter limestone because of calcium carbonate, but granite strong pass am. Na why limestone go small and get holes while granite go still stand well.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes weathering from mass movement?
o: Weathering and mass movement are two names for the same process
Weathering breaks down rocks in situ, while mass movement is the downslope transfer of the weathered material under gravity
Weathering involves transport of broken rock material to new locations, while mass movement breaks rocks in place
Weathering only occurs on steep slopes, while mass movement occurs only on flat land
questions.e: Weathering is the in-place breakdown of rocks by physical, chemical or biological agents, while mass movement is the actual downhill shifting of the loosened material due to gravity. These are related but distinct processes.
questions.p: Weathering na when rock scatter for where e dey, while mass movement na when gravity carry that scattered sand and rock go down slope. Dem be two different things.

questions.q: During road construction along a hilly stretch near Akure, engineers cut into a slope and removed its base support. A few weeks later, after a period of heavy rain, a large mass of rock and soil suddenly broke away and slid rapidly down the exposed slope, causing damage to the road below. This event is best classified as a case of which type of mass movement?
questions.e: A landslide is a rapid, sudden downslope movement of a large mass of rock and soil, often triggered by slope undercutting and heavy rainfall reducing friction. Soil creep is slow and gradual, solifluction occurs mainly in cold regions with thawing ground, and subsidence refers to sinking rather than sliding.
questions.p: When heavy rain fall and rock plus soil rush come down sharp-sharp from cut slope, na landslide be that. Soil creep dey slow, but landslide dey happen quick-quick.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of frost action (freeze-thaw weathering) as a form of mechanical weathering?
o: Rainwater reacting with rock minerals to form a new soft mineral
Daily heating and cooling of bare rock surfaces causing outer layers to peel off
Water entering rock cracks freezes, expands, and widens the cracks until the rock splits apart
Plant roots growing into rock joints and prying them apart over time
questions.e: Frost action occurs when water trapped in rock cracks freezes, expands by about nine percent in volume, and exerts pressure that splits the rock. Root action, exfoliation from heating and cooling, and chemical reactions are different weathering processes.
questions.p: Frost action happen when water enter rock crack, turn to ice, expand, and break the rock. Na mechanical weathering be that, no be chemical reaction.

questions.q: A river valley in its youthful stage is best described as having which of the following cross-sectional shapes?
o: A steep-sided, narrow, V-shaped valley with no floodplain
A shallow, saucer-shaped depression with gentle sides
A broad U-shaped valley with a flat floor
A wide, flat-bottomed valley with gently sloping sides
questions.e: In the youthful stage, vertical (downward) erosion dominates over lateral erosion, producing a narrow, steep-sided V-shaped valley. Floodplains and wide valleys only develop later in the river's course.
questions.p: For the beginning stage of river, water dey cut down ground pass side-side, naim dey make the valley narrow and look like letter V. Na later life of river wide plain and flat valley dey show.

questions.q: Potholes found on the rocky bed of a river in its upper course are mainly formed by which process?
o: Chemical solution of limestone by river water
Grinding and drilling action of pebbles swirled round by eddying water
Deposition of sand and gravel in hollows
Freeze-thaw weathering of the river bank
questions.e: Potholes form when pebbles and stones trapped in small depressions are spun round by turbulent, eddying water, drilling and grinding the depression deeper. This is an abrasive (corrasion) process, not solution or deposition.
questions.p: Pothole dey form when small stones and water dey spin round inside hole, dey grind and bore the rock deep down. Na abrasion process be this, no be say chemical solution or deposition cause am.

questions.q: A river approaching the sea splits into several diverging channels, each dropping its load of silt and sand to build a low, fan-shaped landform at its mouth. This landform is called a
questions.e: A delta is the fan-shaped deposit of sediment formed where a sediment-laden river splits into distributary channels as it enters a sea or lake with weak currents. Levees, waterfalls and gorges are different landforms found elsewhere along a river's course.
questions.p: Delta na the fan-shaped sand deposit wey river dey leave for mouth as e enter sea. Levee, waterfall and gorge na different things wey dey happen for other place for river body.

questions.q: An oxbow lake is formed through which sequence of events?
o: A delta channel is blocked by sandbars and silt builds up across it
A waterfall retreats upstream leaving a plunge pool behind
A river terrace is left standing above the new floodplain level
A meander neck is cut through by the river, and the abandoned loop is sealed off by deposition
questions.e: An oxbow lake results when the narrow neck of a very tight meander is finally breached, so the river takes the shorter straight path. Deposition at the entrances then seals off the abandoned loop, leaving a crescent-shaped lake.
questions.p: Oxbow lake dey happen when river cut short path through tight bend, con leave the old loop make sand block am. Na im make water stay for there as crescent lake.

questions.q: A certain river shows the following features along its length: steep gradient and interlocking spurs near its source, a wide floodplain with meanders in its middle section, and a delta where it meets the sea. This description illustrates the concept of
o: the long profile and the stages of a river's course
questions.e: The changing features from source to mouth (youthful, mature and old stages) describe the river's long profile and the characteristic landforms of each stage. Rejuvenation refers to renewed erosion from uplift or sea-level fall, which is not described here.
questions.p: How river change features from where e start reach where e end dey explain the long profile and stages of river. Rejuvenation mean say river dey start to cut ground afresh because land rise or sea level fall.

questions.q: Two rivers with headwaters close together on opposite sides of a ridge both erode backwards (headward erosion). Eventually the more powerful river's headwater cuts through the ridge and diverts the flow of the weaker river into its own channel. This process is known as
questions.e: River capture (river piracy) occurs when a more actively eroding river extends its valley headward through a watershed and diverts the headwaters of a neighbouring, less powerful river into its own system. Braiding and waterfall retreat describe unrelated river processes.
questions.p: River capture dey happen when strong river cut pass ridge to steal water from another weak river. Braiding and waterfall retreat no be the same thing at all.

questions.q: A river channel divides into several shallow, interweaving channels separated by small islands of sand and gravel, typically because the river is carrying more sediment than it can transport in a single channel. This pattern of channel is called
questions.e: Braiding occurs when a river, overloaded with coarse sediment and having variable discharge, deposits material within its channel, splitting the flow into multiple interweaving shallow channels around small islands (bars). Meanders are single winding channels, while gorges and estuaries are different features.
questions.p: Braided channel dey happen when river carry sand pass wetin e fit push, con scatter water into plenty small-small weaving paths. Meander na just one winding channel, while gorge and estuary different.

questions.q: A deep bowl-shaped depression in a desert, formed mainly through the action of wind deflation and sometimes aided by solution weathering of rock, is known as a
questions.e: A blowout or deflation hollow is formed when wind removes loose, fine material from the surface, leaving a shallow to deep depression. Yardangs and zeugen are ridge-like features, not hollows.
questions.p: Blowout or deflation hollow na when wind carry sand comot from ground make the place deep. Yardang and zeugen na ridge-like features, no be hollow.

questions.q: Which of the following landforms is produced when a glacier erodes a former river valley, widening and deepening it into a distinctive U-shape with steep sides and a flat floor?
questions.e: Glacial troughs are formed when moving ice erodes a river valley, straightening and deepening it into a broad U-shape. V-shaped valleys and gorges are typically river-formed, while rift valleys result from faulting.
questions.p: Glacial trough na when ice widen and deepen river valley to U-shape. V-shaped valleys and gorges na water dey form them, while rift valleys na faulting cause am.

questions.q: On a stretch of Nigerian coastline, a ridge of sand lying roughly parallel to the shore, separated from the mainland by a shallow lagoon, has been built up by wave action over time. This landform is best described as a
questions.e: A barrier bar is a ridge of sand or shingle that runs parallel to the coast and encloses a lagoon between it and the mainland. A spit is attached to the land at one end only, while a tombolo links the mainland to an island.
questions.p: Barrier bar na sand ridge wey dey parallel to coast and keep lagoon for middle. Spit join land for one side only, and tombolo join mainland to island.

questions.q: In a hot desert, wind-transported sand grains bounce and strike exposed rock close to the ground more frequently than higher up. Over a long period, this uneven abrasion is most likely to produce a rock pillar that is
o: narrower at the base than at the top (mushroom-shaped)
wider at the base than at the top
pointed sharply at both the top and the base
questions.e: Because sand grains are concentrated near the ground during wind transport, abrasion is strongest at the base, wearing it narrower while the top remains broader, producing a mushroom-shaped rock (zeugen-like pedestal). This is a classic effect of wind abrasion height distribution.
questions.p: Because sand grains dey ground level pass, wind abrasion go cut base small small make am narrow. This one dey form mushroom-shaped rock.

questions.q: A valley that was once occupied by a glacier now has several smaller valleys entering it from the sides, but these smaller valleys end abruptly high up on the walls of the main valley, with streams often falling as waterfalls into it. The main valley is called a
questions.e: The main glacier erodes its valley floor much deeper than the smaller tributary glaciers, so after the ice melts, the tributary valleys are left hanging above the main valley floor, often with waterfalls. This is a well-known feature of glaciated highland regions.
questions.p: Main glacier dey deep pass small tributary glaciers, so when ice melt, the small valleys dey hang high up. Na so hanging valleys dey happen.

questions.q: Along a coast, waves approach a headland from the open sea and bend around it before striking the shore. This bending of waves as they move into shallower water near the headland is called
questions.e: Wave refraction occurs when waves slow down in shallower water near a headland and bend to align more closely with the shape of the coastline. Longshore drift is the movement of sediment along the coast, which is a different process.
questions.p: Wave refraction na when waves slow down for shallow water near headland and bend. Longshore drift na movement of sand along coast, wey be different thing.
