questions.q: A broad, gently sloping surface of exposed bedrock found at the foot of mountains in a desert region, formed mainly by the combined action of sheet flooding and wind erosion removing weathered debris, is called a
questions.e: A pediment is a gently sloping rock surface at the base of desert mountains, shaped by sheet floods and wind removing weathered material, leaving a smooth bedrock platform. A playa is a dry lake bed, while a wadi is a dry stream channel, both different features.
questions.p: Pediment na smooth bedrock surface for foot of desert mountain where water and wind don sweep debris comot. Playa na dry lake bed, and wadi na dry channel.

questions.q: A glacier picks up rock fragments as it moves and deposits an unsorted mixture of clay, sand, and boulders directly from the melting ice, without any sorting by water. This unsorted glacial deposit is known as
questions.e: Till, also called boulder clay, is deposited directly by melting ice and contains an unsorted mixture of particle sizes from clay to large boulders. Outwash and alluvium are sorted by flowing water, while loess is wind-blown dust, which is a different process entirely.
questions.p: Till or boulder clay na unsorted mixture of clay, sand and stones wey ice drop directly when e melt. Water dey sort outwash and alluvium, while loess na wind-blown dust.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure the amount of sunshine received at a place?
questions.e: The Campbell-Stokes recorder uses a glass sphere to focus sunlight onto a card, burning a trace that shows the duration of bright sunshine. The other instruments measure temperature housing, humidity and wind speed respectively.
questions.p: Na Campbell-Stokes recorder we dey use glass sphere focus sun light burn line for card to measure how long bright sun shine. Di other instruments dey measure temperature, humidity and wind speed.

questions.q: A Stevenson screen is painted white and raised above the ground mainly in order to
o: increase the weight of the box so wind cannot blow it over
reflect solar radiation and allow free circulation of air around the instruments
make it easy for meteorologists to locate it from a distance
protect the instruments from being stolen by children
questions.e: White paint reflects heat so the box itself does not warm up and affect the readings, while the raised, louvred design allows air to circulate freely for accurate temperature and humidity measurement. The other options are not the scientific reasons for its design.
questions.p: White paint dey reflect heat make di box no hot, and di openings allow air blow well well for correct temperature and humidity reading. Di other reasons no correct for science.

questions.q: Relative humidity is best described as the
o: amount of water vapour a parcel of air can hold at a given temperature before it rains
total weight of water vapour contained in one cubic metre of air regardless of temperature
difference between the dry bulb and wet bulb thermometer readings
ratio of the actual water vapour content of air to the maximum it can hold at that temperature, expressed as a percentage
questions.e: Relative humidity compares the actual moisture in the air with the maximum amount the air could hold at that same temperature, shown as a percentage. The other options describe absolute humidity or the depression of the wet bulb, which are different concepts.
questions.p: Relative humidity be di ratio of actual water vapour inside air compared to di maximum wey di air fit hold for dat temperature, wey we dey write for percentage. Di other options talk about different things like absolute humidity.

questions.q: A town recorded a mean annual temperature of 27°C and a mean annual rainfall of 2200mm with rain falling throughout the year, no month having less than 60mm. This climate is best classified as
questions.e: High uniform temperatures above 25°C with heavy rainfall spread evenly all year and no dry month are the defining features of the equatorial climate. Desert and Mediterranean climates have marked dry seasons, which do not fit this data.
questions.p: High temperature pass 25°C with heavy rain wey dey fall throughout di year without dry month na im be equatorial climate. Desert and Mediterranean climates get dry season wey no match dis data.

questions.q: At the foot of a mountain, the temperature is 30°C. If the normal lapse rate of 6.5°C per 1000 metres is applied, what will be the approximate temperature at a height of 2000 metres on the mountain?
questions.e: Temperature falls by about 6.5°C for every 1000 metres risen, so at 2000 metres the fall is 13°C, giving 30°C minus 13°C which equals 17°C. This calculation uses the environmental lapse rate to find temperature change with altitude.
questions.p: Temperature dey drop by 6.5°C for every 1000 metres wey person climb, so for 2000 metres di drop na 13°C, wey mean say 30°C minus 13°C give us 17°C. Dis na how we dey calculate lapse rate.

questions.q: A meteorological station recorded a dry bulb temperature of 26°C and a wet bulb temperature of 20°C. What does the large difference of 6°C between the two readings indicate about the air at that time?
o: The air is fully saturated with water vapour
The air is very dry with low relative humidity
The wind speed is very strong
The air pressure is unusually high
questions.e: A large gap between the dry bulb and wet bulb readings means a lot of water evaporated from the wet bulb's wick, cooling it significantly, which only happens when the surrounding air is dry and can absorb much moisture. If the air were saturated, both thermometers would show almost the same reading.
questions.p: Big difference between dry and wet bulb temperature mean say water dey evaporate fast because di air dry well well. If di air full of moisture, both thermometers for show almost di same reading.

questions.q: Which of these correctly lists factors that together determine the climate of a place, as distinct from the day to day elements of weather?
o: Rainfall, temperature, humidity and air pressure
Temperature, rainfall, sunshine and wind speed
Latitude, altitude, distance from the sea and ocean currents
Humidity, cloud cover, pressure and visibility
questions.e: Latitude, altitude, nearness to the sea and ocean currents are controls that influence the general climate pattern of a region over a long period. The other lists name weather elements, which are short term atmospheric conditions, not climatic controls.
questions.p: Latitude, altitude, distance from sea and ocean currents na im be di factors wey dey control climate over long time. Di other lists na just short term weather elements.

questions.q: A town has a mean annual rainfall of 650 mm, concentrated mainly in winter, with hot, dry summers where temperatures can exceed 30°C. Olive and citrus cultivation are common. Which climate type is being described?
questions.e: Hot dry summers with rain concentrated in winter and olive/citrus farming are classic features of the Mediterranean (warm temperate western margin) climate. The other climates do not have this winter-rain, summer-drought pattern.
questions.p: Hot dry summer with rain wey dey fall for winter time and olive/citrus farming na true true sign of Mediterranean climate. Na only dis climate dey get dis kind winter-rain and summer-drought pattern.

questions.q: Which pair of climatic elements is most commonly used as the basis for classifying world climates into types such as equatorial, tropical continental, and cool temperate?
questions.e: Climate classification systems group regions mainly by their temperature patterns and rainfall amount/distribution throughout the year. Pressure, humidity, altitude and latitude may influence climate but are not the main classifying elements.
questions.p: To classify world climates, geography people dey use temperature pattern and how rainfall dey spread across the year. Other things like pressure and wind fit influence am, but temperature and rainfall na the main things.

questions.q: Which of the following is the main reason cool temperate continental interior climates (such as those found deep inside large landmasses) experience a very large annual temperature range?
o: High amounts of rainfall throughout the year
Presence of warm ocean currents nearby
Distance from the moderating influence of the sea
questions.e: Land heats up and cools down faster than the sea, so places far inland lack the sea's moderating effect, giving hot summers and very cold winters. Nearness to the equator, heavy year-round rainfall and warm currents would instead reduce the temperature range.
questions.p: Land dey hot and cold quick quick pass water, so places wey dey deep inside landmass no dey see sea help them moderate temperature. Dis one dey make summer hot well well and winter very cold.

questions.q: A geography class is told that a certain climate type has cool summers, cold winters with snow, coniferous forest vegetation, and is found roughly between latitudes 50°N and 70°N across Canada and Siberia. This describes the
questions.e: Cool summers, very cold snowy winters and coniferous (taiga) forest at high latitudes across Canada and Siberia describe the boreal/cool temperate continental climate. The other options describe warmer or coastal climates that do not fit this description.
questions.p: Cool summer, cold winter with snow and coniferous forest for Canada and Siberia na the correct way wey dem dey describe boreal or cool temperate continental climate. Na only dis climate fit dis description.

questions.q: A coastal city lying between latitudes 50°N and 60°N receives rain in every month of the year, has mild winters rarely below 2°C, and cool summers rarely above 18°C, due to the influence of a warm ocean current offshore. Which climate type does this best represent?
o: Cool temperate western margin (British type) climate
questions.e: Rain all year, mild winters and cool summers under the influence of warm currents at these mid-to-high latitudes are typical of the cool temperate western margin (British type) climate. Mediterranean has dry summers, monsoon is tropical, and deserts have very little rainfall.
questions.p: Rain every month, mild winter and cool summer because of warm ocean current na the true true character of cool temperate western margin or British type climate. Mediterranean get dry summer, while desert dry pass.

questions.q: In a particular region, rainfall exceeds 2,000 mm annually and falls fairly evenly across the year, mean monthly temperatures stay between 24°C and 28°C with almost no seasonal variation, and tropical rainforest vegetation thrives. A student wrongly classifies this as a tropical monsoon climate instead of equatorial. What is the strongest reason this classification is wrong?
o: Monsoon climates occur only in desert interiors far from the coast
Monsoon climates always receive less total rainfall than equatorial regions
Monsoon climates have lower temperatures throughout the year than equatorial regions
Monsoon climates have a well-marked dry season caused by seasonal reversal of winds, which is absent here
questions.e: The key distinguishing feature of monsoon climates is a strong wet-dry seasonal contrast driven by reversing winds, which is missing in the region described, where rain is spread evenly all year as in equatorial climates. The other options misstate facts about rainfall totals, location and temperature of monsoon climates.
questions.p: Monsoon climate must get dry season because wind dey change direction, but dis place wey rain dey fall all through year na equatorial climate. Monsoon climate no be like dat because e get proper dry season.

questions.q: The coniferous forest belt (taiga), stretching across Northern Canada, Scandinavia and Siberia, is dominated by trees such as pine, spruce and fir. Which of the following best explains why these trees have narrow, needle-shaped leaves?
o: To reduce water loss and withstand heavy snow load during long cold winters
To absorb more sunlight during the brief periods of darkness
To increase the rate of photosynthesis during the short summer
To attract more insects for pollination throughout the year
questions.e: Needle-shaped leaves have a small surface area, which reduces transpiration in the dry cold winter and allows snow to slide off easily. This is an adaptation to the harsh, cold, dry conditions of the taiga climate.
questions.p: Needle-shaped leaves get small surface area, so water no dey commot quick. E still dey help snow make e slide commot so the tree no go break for cold winter.

questions.q: A student observes that a particular soil type is sandy, very thin, poorly developed and almost without organic matter, found on steep rocky slopes where erosion is rapid and weathering has barely begun. This soil is best classified as a(n)
questions.e: Azonal soils are young, shallow and poorly developed because erosion or deposition prevents proper horizon formation. They are common on steep slopes and are not controlled mainly by climate, unlike zonal soils.
questions.p: Azonal soils na young soil wey no get proper layer because erosion dey disturb am. Dem no dey depend on climate like zonal soils, na why dem dey common for steep slopes.

questions.q: Steppe (temperate grassland) vegetation, found in regions such as the Eurasian plains, differs from tropical savanna mainly in that steppe
o: consists mainly of short grasses with few or no trees due to low rainfall and cold winters
is found only near the equator where temperatures are constantly high
occurs in areas with hot wet summers and heavy year-round rainfall
has scattered trees mixed with tall elephant grass
questions.e: Steppe grassland grows in temperate interior regions with low rainfall and cold winters, so it lacks trees and consists of short grasses. This distinguishes it from the tropical savanna, which has tall grass and scattered trees under a hot climate.
questions.p: Steppe grassland dey grow for place wey rain no too fall and winter dey cold, so tree no fit grow there. Na only short grass dey, unlike savanna wey get tall grass and tree.

questions.q: In the tropical rainforest, a distinct feature is the arrangement of trees into different heights forming layers, with the tallest trees rising above the general canopy. What is this layered structure called?
questions.e: Stratification refers to the arrangement of forest vegetation into distinct layers, such as emergent trees, canopy, understorey and ground layer. This layering is a key identifying feature of tropical rainforest structure.
questions.p: Stratification mean say forest get different layers like canopy and undergrowth. Na this arrangement make rainforest look like say e get levels.

questions.q: A geography field report describes a tropical soil that is deep, intensely leached, rich in iron and aluminium oxides, poor in plant nutrients, and which hardens irreversibly into a brick-like material when repeatedly exposed to the sun after vegetation is cleared. This process of hardening is called
questions.e: Laterisation is the process by which exposed tropical soils, rich in iron and aluminium oxides, harden into a tough brick-like crust on repeated drying by the sun. This differs from podzolisation, which occurs in cold coniferous regions, and from salinisation, which involves salt accumulation.
questions.p: Laterisation na when tropical soil wey get iron and aluminium oxide dry under sun and turn hard like brick. This one different from other soil process because of how e dey harden.

questions.q: Tundra vegetation, found in the Arctic regions beyond the taiga, is characterised mainly by mosses, lichens and small shrubs rather than tall trees. The main climatic reason for the absence of tall trees in this region is
o: a permanently frozen subsoil and very short, cool growing season
strong ocean currents that erode tree roots constantly
extremely high temperatures that scorch tree roots
excessive rainfall causing waterlogging throughout the year
questions.e: The tundra has permafrost, a permanently frozen layer below the surface, and only a very short cool summer for growth. These conditions prevent deep root growth and the development of tall trees, favouring mosses, lichens and dwarf shrubs instead.
questions.p: Tundra get permafrost, meaning ground dey frozen always, and summer time too short. Tree no fit grow long root for there, so na only moss and small shrub fit survive.

questions.q: Chidinma is studying a world vegetation map and notices a belt of short, tough, drought-resistant shrubs with thick waxy leaves located on the western margins of continents between about 30° and 40° North and South, where summers are hot and dry while winters are mild and wet. This vegetation type is known as
questions.e: Mediterranean scrub, also called maquis, consists of drought-resistant shrubs with thick waxy leaves adapted to hot dry summers and mild wet winters. This vegetation is typical of the 30 to 40 degree latitude belts on the western sides of continents.
questions.p: Mediterranean scrub get tough leaves to survive hot dry summer and mild wet winter. You go see this kind vegetation for western side of continents for 30 to 40 degree latitude.

questions.q: A soil scientist studying a tropical black soil (vertisol) formed from basaltic parent rock in a region with marked wet and dry seasons notes that the soil develops deep cracks during the dry season as it shrinks, then swells and closes up again when wet. This swelling and shrinking behaviour is mainly due to the soil's high content of
o: Clay minerals that absorb and release water
questions.e: Vertisols are rich in expanding clay minerals that absorb water and swell in the wet season, then shrink and crack as they dry out. This shrink-swell behaviour, not sand, humus or calcium carbonate, is the defining property of these black tropical soils.
questions.p: Vertisols get special clay wey dey swell when rain fall and shrink when sun hot. This movement na wetin dey cause the deep cracks wey you dey see for the ground.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines environmental conservation?
o: The total removal of human activities from forest reserves
The process of converting renewable resources into non-renewable ones
The wise use and management of natural resources to prevent waste and ensure continued availability for future generations
The exploration of mineral resources without any form of restriction
questions.e: Conservation means managing resources carefully so they are not wasted and remain available for future use. The other options describe harmful or unrelated practices, not conservation.
questions.p: Conservation na to manage wetin we get well-well so e no go finish. We dey do am so say our children go still see am use for future.

questions.q: A certain forest reserve covers 2,400 hectares. If 15% of the reserve is cleared yearly for farming without replanting, how many hectares will be left after 2 years, assuming the same percentage of the remaining land is cleared each year?
questions.e: After year one, 2400 - (0.15 x 2400) = 2040 hectares remain. After year two, 2040 - (0.15 x 2040) = 1734 hectares remain. This shows compound depletion rather than a flat rate.
questions.p: After year one, 2400 minus 15 percent remain 2040 hectares. For year two, we come remove 15 percent from that 2040, so 1734 hectares remain.

questions.q: In the context of environmental hazards, which of the following is best classified as a man-made (human-induced) hazard rather than a natural hazard?
questions.e: Oil spillage from industrial activities results directly from human actions such as poor equipment maintenance or sabotage. Volcanic eruptions, tsunamis and earthquakes occur due to natural earth processes.
questions.p: Oil spillage na human work because na machine or person error dey cause am. But volcano, tsunami and earthquake na natural tin wey dey happen by itself.

questions.q: Overgrazing by livestock in the Sahelian grasslands leads most directly to which of the following environmental consequences?
o: Increased rainfall and humidity in the region
Rapid growth of dense rainforest vegetation
Loss of vegetation cover and exposure of soil to wind erosion
questions.e: When too many animals graze an area, they strip away grass cover faster than it can regrow, leaving bare soil exposed to erosion by wind. This does not cause increased rainfall or forest growth.
questions.p: If animal too plenty for one place, dem go chop all grass finish. When grass no dey, wind go come carry the soil go, wey we dey call erosion.

questions.q: A community wishes to conserve its freshwater resources for the dry season. Which of the following practices would best achieve this goal?
o: Allowing unrestricted discharge of untreated waste into rivers
Digging boreholes without any plan for recharge of the water table
Constructing small dams and reservoirs to harvest and store rainwater during the wet season
Clearing all vegetation along riverbanks to increase water flow speed
questions.e: Building dams and reservoirs captures excess rainwater during the wet season so it can be used later when water is scarce. The other options either waste water, pollute it, or deplete groundwater without replenishment.
questions.p: To build dam na better way to keep water for dry season. If you keep water when rain dey fall, you go get wetin you go use when sun hot.

questions.q: Which pair correctly matches an environmental hazard with an appropriate mitigation measure?
o: Flooding — construction of drainage channels and embankments along rivers
Drought — removal of windbreaks around farmlands
Erosion — ploughing land along the slope instead of across it
Landslide — increasing deforestation on steep slopes
questions.e: Drainage channels and embankments control excess water flow and reduce flood damage. The other pairings describe actions that would worsen, not reduce, the stated hazards.
questions.p: Drainage and embankment dey help control water so flood no go too spoil property. Other ones wey dem list go only make the problem worse.

questions.q: A farmland on a hillside experiences severe soil loss whenever it rains heavily. Which combination of conservation techniques would most effectively reduce this soil loss?
o: Ploughing the land in straight lines down the slope
Increasing the number of grazing animals on the slope
Removing all tree stumps and leaving the soil bare between seasons
Terracing the slope and planting cover crops
questions.e: Terracing breaks a steep slope into flat steps that slow down water runoff, while cover crops hold the soil together with their roots, both reducing erosion. Bare soil, downslope ploughing and overgrazing all increase the speed and damage of runoff.
questions.p: Terracing dey make slope look like step so water no go run fast. If you plant cover crops too, the root go hold the soil make e no wash comot.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why wetlands are considered valuable environmental resources worth conserving?
o: They serve mainly as sites for heavy industrial construction
They filter pollutants from water, provide habitats for wildlife, and help control flooding by absorbing excess water
They prevent all forms of rainfall from reaching the ground surface
They produce large quantities of crude oil for industrial use
questions.e: Wetlands act as natural filters, support diverse wildlife, and absorb excess rainwater, reducing the risk of flooding downstream. They are not sources of crude oil, nor are they suited for industrial construction.
questions.p: Wetlands dey clean water and give house to many animals. Dem also dey soak excess water so flood no go too disturb people.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of environmental resources are both classified as flow (perpetual) resources because they are continuously renewed by natural processes and cannot be exhausted by human use?
questions.e: Solar energy and wind energy are flow resources because they are continuously supplied by nature and are never used up no matter how much is tapped. The other pairs are mineral or fossil resources that are limited in supply and take a very long time to form.
questions.p: Solar energy and wind energy na flow resources because nature dey supply dem continuous and dem no dey finish no matter how man use am. Di other pairs na minerals and fossil fuels wey get limit and dey take plenty years to form.

questions.q: In the management of environmental hazards, the term 'mitigation' refers mainly to
o: the process of rescuing victims immediately after a disaster strikes
actions taken to reduce the severity or impact of a hazard before it occurs
the total abandonment of a hazard-prone area by its residents
the scientific study of how hazards are formed in nature
questions.e: Mitigation means taking steps beforehand, such as building flood defences or enforcing building codes, to lessen the damage a hazard can cause. Rescue operations and relocation are separate aspects of disaster management, not mitigation itself.
questions.p: Mitigation mean to take steps before disaster happen, like to build flood defence or follow building rules, so that damage go reduce. Rescue and moving away na different part of disaster management, no be mitigation.

questions.q: A state government wants to prevent the drying up of a reservoir that supplies water to a city. Which combination of measures would best conserve the water catchment area feeding the reservoir?
o: Constructing more boreholes upstream to reduce pressure on the reservoir
Clearing the vegetation around the catchment to create more farmland for food security
Protecting the forest cover around the catchment and restricting bush burning near the reservoir
Allowing unrestricted grazing of cattle within the catchment to boost livestock production
questions.e: Vegetation around a catchment reduces surface runoff, controls erosion and helps maintain the water table, so protecting it and preventing bush burning conserves the water supply. Clearing land, overgrazing or sinking more boreholes upstream would instead worsen siltation and reduce the reservoir's water level.
questions.p: Plant and trees for catchment area dey help hold water and stop erosion, so to protect forest and stop bush burning go help water supply. If you clear land or put too many cow, water go dry quick.

questions.q: A coastal town experiences rising sea levels that are gradually submerging low-lying farmlands. This situation is best classified under which category of environmental hazard?
questions.e: Rising sea levels are linked to climate change and changing weather and climatic patterns, making it a climatic hazard. It is not caused by living organisms, earth movements, or industrial technology, so the other options do not fit.
questions.p: As sea level dey rise, na because of climate change and weather pattern, so na climatic hazard. Na nottin concern living things, earth movement, or machine technology for here.

questions.q: A game reserve has a fixed carrying capacity of 500 elephants based on available vegetation and water. If the elephant population grows at a steady rate of 40 elephants per year from an initial population of 300, after how many years will the reserve reach its carrying capacity, assuming no elephants leave or die?
questions.e: The population needs to grow by 500 minus 300, which is 200 elephants, and growing at 40 elephants per year means 200 divided by 40 equals 5 years. This shows how exceeding carrying capacity through unchecked population growth can threaten a reserve's resources.
questions.p: To reach 500 elephants from 300, you need 200 more elephants, and since dem dey grow 40 elephants every year, 200 divide by 40 give you 5 years. This show how too much population fit spoil reserve resource.

questions.q: In a certain farming region, deforestation has increased surface runoff so that a river which used to flood only once every 10 years now floods on average once every 2 years. By what factor has the flooding frequency increased as a result of deforestation?
questions.e: The flooding frequency changed from once in 10 years to once in 2 years, and dividing 10 by 2 gives 5, meaning floods now occur 5 times more often. This illustrates how removing vegetation cover through deforestation increases runoff and worsens flood hazards.
questions.p: Before, flood dey happen once in 10 years, but now e dey happen once in 2 years, and if you divide 10 by 2, you go get 5. This one show say cutting down trees dey make flood happen 5 times more pass before.

questions.q: A region in the Niger Delta has rich crude oil deposits, swampy terrain, high humidity and frequent flooding. Based on these physical conditions, the population of this region is most likely to be:
o: Evenly distributed across the entire region
Sparsely distributed due to difficult terrain and flooding
Densely distributed because of oil wealth alone
questions.e: Swampy land, high humidity and flooding make settlement, farming and movement difficult, so such areas tend to have low population density despite mineral wealth. People avoid hazardous, waterlogged terrain for permanent settlement.
questions.p: Swampy place, heat, and water no allow person build house or farm well. Even though oil dey there, people no too like stay for waterlogged area.

questions.q: In a particular year, 28,000 people moved into Ogun State from other states while 16,000 people moved out of Ogun State to other states. What is the net migration figure for Ogun State for that year?
questions.e: Net migration is calculated as in-migrants minus out-migrants: 28,000 minus 16,000 equals 12,000. Since more people entered than left, this is net in-migration.
questions.p: To find net migration, just minus people wey commot from people wey enter. 28,000 minus 16,000 na 12,000, and since more people enter, na net in-migration.

questions.q: A geography teacher explains that a country's population may increase even when its birth rate and death rate are both falling steadily. Which factor best accounts for this situation?
o: A rise in the crude death rate above the birth rate
An increase in the rate of emigration
A large net in-migration of foreigners into the country
A fall in life expectancy at birth
questions.e: Population growth depends on natural increase (births minus deaths) plus net migration. Even with falling birth and death rates, strong in-migration can still push total population upward.
questions.p: Population fit still increase if plenty foreigners pack come inside the country. Even if birth and death rate dey fall, strong in-migration go push the total number up.

questions.q: Study this scenario: Country X has a youthful population with a broad base and narrow top when its age-sex structure is drawn, while Country Y has a population pyramid with a narrow base and a wide middle and top. Which statement correctly compares their likely population growth rates?
o: Country X will grow faster because it has many young people entering reproductive age
Country Y will grow faster because it has more elderly dependents
Both countries will have identical growth rates regardless of pyramid shape
Country X will decline because narrow tops indicate high mortality
questions.e: A broad-based pyramid shows a large young population that will soon enter childbearing age, driving future population growth. A narrow base, as in Country Y, suggests low birth rates and slower or declining growth.
questions.p: Country wey get broad base mean say dem get plenty young people wey go soon born pikin. Naim make Country X go grow fast pass Country Y wey get narrow base.

questions.q: A survey shows that a Nigerian city's population grew from 800,000 to 968,000 in exactly one year, entirely due to migration (no natural increase recorded). What was the percentage growth in population caused by migration that year?
questions.e: Percentage growth equals the increase (968,000 minus 800,000 = 168,000) divided by the original population (800,000), multiplied by 100, giving 21%. This shows how migration alone can noticeably raise city population.
questions.p: If you minus 800,000 from 968,000, you go get 168,000 increase. Divide am by 800,000 and times 100, you go get 21% percent.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major CONSEQUENCE of rapid rural-urban migration commonly experienced in Nigerian cities such as Lagos and Port Harcourt?
o: Decline in demand for housing within the city
Increase in agricultural labour supply in the city
Growth of slums and pressure on social amenities
questions.e: When too many migrants arrive in cities faster than infrastructure can expand, slums develop and amenities like water, schools and hospitals become overstretched. This is a well-documented effect of rapid rural-urban migration in Nigeria.
questions.p: When people too plenty for city, slum go grow and wahala for light, water, and house go surface. Na wetin fast rural-urban migration dey cause for Nigeria.

questions.q: A town originally grew as a river-crossing point where traders paused to exchange goods, and this trading role later became its main reason for continued growth, overtaking its original importance as a crossing point. This situation best illustrates which settlement concept?
questions.e: When a settlement's original purpose for growth is replaced by a new dominant activity, geographers call this a change of function. The crossing point role gave way to a trading function as the town developed.
questions.p: When town change wetin e dey do before come start do anoda work, we dey call am change of function. The town start as crossing point but as e grow, trading come become the main thing wey dey make am big.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important factor responsible for the dispersed (scattered) settlement pattern common in areas of forest clearing and shifting cultivation in parts of Nigeria?
o: Presence of a central market square
Availability of large areas of farmland around each homestead
questions.e: In shifting cultivation areas, each family needs a large piece of land to farm and clear, so houses are built far apart near their farmlands. This spacing produces a dispersed settlement pattern.
questions.p: For places where dem dey do shifting cultivation, every family need big land to farm. Because of this, houses dey far from each oda, wey come make the settlement look scattered.

questions.q: In central place theory, which of the following best explains why a large town can support a specialist hospital and a university while a nearby small village can only support a primary school and a small market?
o: The village has no roads linking it to other places
The large town has a bigger range and threshold population to support higher-order services
The large town was founded earlier in history
The village population refuses to pay taxes
questions.e: Higher-order services like hospitals and universities need a large threshold population and wider range of customers to remain viable. Only large towns usually have enough people to support such services, while villages can only sustain low-order functions.
questions.p: Big services like university need plenty people to survive, wey we dey call threshold population. Big towns get enough people to support these things, but small villages no get that kind population.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a settlement pattern with its typical description?
o: Radial pattern - houses scattered randomly with no relationship to roads
Dispersed pattern - houses tightly packed in rows along a highway
Nucleated pattern - houses closely grouped together around a central point such as a market or water source
Linear pattern - houses spread evenly in a circular arrangement around a hill
questions.e: A nucleated pattern is one where houses and buildings cluster closely together, usually around a focal point like a market, church, or water source. The other options wrongly describe linear, dispersed and radial patterns.
questions.p: Nucleated pattern mean say houses dey gather together for one place. Dem fit gather round market or water source for protection or easy access.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why many traditional settlements in Northern Nigeria were originally built in nucleated form, with houses clustered together and surrounded by a wall or fence?
o: To provide collective defence against raids and attacks
To reduce the cost of building roads
To make trading with distant towns easier
To allow each family unlimited farmland
questions.e: In the past, communities clustered their houses together, often behind walls, mainly for protection and collective defence against raiders. This defensive need was a major historical reason for nucleated settlement patterns in many parts of Northern Nigeria.
questions.p: Before, people for Northern Nigeria dey build house together and put wall round am for protection. This one help dem defend demselves well against people wey wan attack dem.

questions.q: A geographer classifies a settlement as 'urban' rather than 'rural' mainly on the basis of which combination of characteristics?
o: Large population size, high density of buildings, and dominance of non-agricultural occupations
Scattered houses and low literacy levels
Small population size and total dependence on farming
Presence of a village head and a single primary school
questions.e: Urban settlements are generally identified by large population size, high building density, and a dominance of non-farming activities such as trade, industry, and services. Rural settlements, by contrast, are smaller and mostly agricultural.
questions.p: Urban settlement get plenty people, many buildings, and people no dey do farming as main work. Rural settlement small and most people dey do farming.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State practises a system in which crops such as yam, maize and cassava are planted together on the same piece of land at the same time. This farming practice is best described as
questions.e: Growing two or more different crops together on the same plot at the same time is called mixed cropping. Mixed farming instead combines crop growing with animal rearing.
questions.p: E dey called mixed cropping when person plant different crops together for one land for the same time. Mixed farming na when person dey do crop planting join animal rearing.

questions.q: Which of the following is the chief advantage of mechanized agriculture over traditional hand-tool farming in Nigeria?
o: It makes land more suitable for shifting cultivation
It eliminates the need for fertilizer use
It increases output per worker by cultivating larger areas quickly
questions.e: Machines such as tractors allow fewer workers to cultivate much larger farmlands within a short time, raising output per worker. Mechanization actually requires heavy capital investment, not less.
questions.p: With machines like tractor, small worker fit farm big big land sharp sharp, and dis one dey increase wet worker dey produce. But make we know say machine cost money well well to buy.

questions.q: A tin-mining company in Jos extracted 1,800 tonnes of ore in a year. If 15% of the ore was lost as waste during processing, how many tonnes of usable ore remained?
questions.e: 15% of 1,800 is 270 tonnes lost as waste. Subtracting 270 from 1,800 leaves 1,530 tonnes of usable ore.
questions.p: If 15% of 1,800 na 270 tonnes wey waste, when you minus am, wet remain na 1,530 tonnes of usable ore. Na simple math be dat.

questions.q: Open-cast (surface) mining method is most suitable for extracting mineral deposits that are
o: located close to the earth's surface
found deep below thick rock layers
questions.e: Open-cast mining involves removing the topsoil to expose minerals that lie near the surface, making it cheaper than digging deep shafts. Deep-seated minerals require shaft or underground mining instead.
questions.p: Open-cast mining mean say dem go remove top soil to pack minerals wey dey near ground surface, and dis one beta pass to dey dig deep underground. Na only deep minerals dem dey use underground mining for.

questions.q: A major problem associated with artisanal (small-scale local) mining of solid minerals in parts of Nigeria is
o: overproduction leading to falling mineral prices
excessive government regulation preventing any mining activity
environmental damage such as land degradation and water pollution
the total absence of mineral deposits in such areas
questions.e: Artisanal miners often use crude methods without proper environmental control, leading to land degradation, erosion and pollution of nearby water bodies. This is a well-known effect of unregulated small-scale mining.
questions.p: Small-scale miners dey spoil land and water body well well because dem no dey use proper method to control environmental damage. Dis one na big headache for Nigeria areas wey dem dey do mining.

questions.q: Which pair of industries is correctly matched as basic (heavy) industry and consumer-goods (light) industry respectively?
o: Iron and steel industry; textile industry
Soft drink bottling; iron and steel industry
questions.e: Iron and steel production supplies raw materials to other industries, making it a basic industry, while textile manufacturing produces goods used directly by consumers, making it a light industry. The other pairings wrongly classify cement or bakery products.
questions.p: Iron and steel na basic industry because na dem dey supply iron materials to other industries, while textile na light industry wey dey make cloth for people to wear directly.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important reason manufacturing industries are usually sited close to large urban centres such as Lagos and Kano rather than in remote rural villages?
o: Rural areas lack any form of road network
Rural land is more expensive than urban land
Raw materials are only found in cities
Urban centres provide a larger market and better supply of labour and infrastructure
questions.e: Cities offer a ready market for finished goods, a large pool of workers, and infrastructure like electricity, water and transport, all of which reduce production costs. Rural land being cheaper would actually favour rural siting, not the reverse.
questions.p: Towns like Lagos and Kano get plenty market, worker, and beta infrastructure like light and road wey company need to work well. Na dis reasons make industries like to pack go city instead of village.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'entrepot trade' as practised at ports such as Lagos and Lome?
o: Trade in which goods are exchanged by barter without the use of money
Trade in which goods are bought and sold strictly within one country's borders
Trade in which a country re-exports imported goods to other countries after storing them, usually with little or no processing
Trade in which a country manufactures goods solely for its own local consumption
questions.e: Entrepot trade involves importing goods into a central port or country and then re-exporting them to other countries, often after storage but little processing. This is common at busy coastal trading centres.
questions.p: Entrepot trade mean say dem dey bring goods enter port, keep am small, and then carry am go sell for another country. Na so port cities dey do am.

questions.q: Which of these best explains why water transport is generally preferred for international trade in bulky raw materials such as iron ore and timber?
o: It has the shortest travel time compared to all other modes
It requires the least amount of infrastructure to operate
It is the only mode that can cross international boundaries
It offers large carrying capacity at relatively low cost per tonne over long distances
questions.e: Ships can carry very large volumes of bulky goods at a lower cost per tonne than road, rail, or air transport, making water transport ideal for heavy raw materials moved over long distances. Other modes are faster but far more expensive for such bulk cargo.
questions.p: Ship fit carry plenty heavy goods like iron ore and timber for long distance with cheap money per tonne. Na why water transport good pass for bulky cargo.

questions.q: Which factor is most responsible for the relatively low volume of air transport used for moving agricultural produce within Nigeria, compared to road transport?
o: High cost of air transport makes it uneconomical for low-value bulky produce
Air transport cannot legally carry agricultural goods across state borders
There are no airports located near farming areas in Nigeria
Air transport is unsafe for carrying farm produce
questions.e: Air transport is fast but very expensive, making it unsuitable for low-value, bulky goods like most agricultural produce, which cannot bear such high freight charges. Road transport remains cheaper and more accessible for moving farm produce within the country.
questions.p: Air transport cost too much for low-value farm goods wey heavy. Na road transport farmers dey use reach everywhere because e cheap small.

questions.q: A regional trade agreement among West African countries removes tariffs on goods traded among member states but still allows each country to set its own tariffs on goods from non-member countries. This arrangement is best classified as a?
questions.e: A free trade area removes trade barriers like tariffs among member countries while allowing each member to maintain its own independent tariffs against non-members. This differs from a customs union, which requires a common external tariff for all members.
questions.p: Free trade area dey allow member countries trade without tariff, but everybody get their own rule for outside countries. E different from customs union.

questions.q: In the equatorial rainforest belt of southern Nigeria, the vegetation typically shows a distinct layering pattern. Which of the following correctly describes this layering from the ground upward?
o: Grasses only, with scattered stunted trees of equal height
Mosses and lichens, then tall trees of uniform height with no undergrowth
Ground herbs, undergrowth shrubs, then two or three tree canopy layers with emergent trees on top
Herb layer, then a single continuous canopy, then bare soil
questions.e: Tropical rainforest in southern Nigeria is stratified into ground herbs, shrubby undergrowth, and multiple tree canopy layers, with some emergent trees rising above the rest. The other options describe savanna-type or unrealistic structures, not rainforest.
questions.p: Tropical rainforest for southern Nigeria dey get strata from ground herbs, shrubby undergrowth, and multiple tree canopy layers, with some emergent trees wey dey rise pass the rest. Na only this option correct as rainforest structure.

questions.q: A town in central Nigeria receives rainfall mainly between April and October, with a short period of harmattan dust haze around December to January, and total annual rainfall of about 1300 mm. This climate description best matches which climatic zone of Nigeria?
o: The tropical continental (savanna) climate of the Guinea savanna belt
The mangrove swamp climate of the Niger Delta
The equatorial monsoon climate of the Niger Delta coastline
The semi-arid climate of the Sahel near Lake Chad
questions.e: A single wet season from April to October, a noticeable harmattan period, and moderate rainfall around 1300 mm are typical of the Guinea savanna climate found in Nigeria's middle belt. The Sahel is drier with less rainfall, while the Delta and coastline have much higher, more evenly spread rainfall.
questions.p: Wet season from April to October, harmattan period, and moderate rainfall around 1300 mm na character of Guinea savanna climate for Nigeria middle belt. Other options no match these weather condition at all.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly compares the temperature regimes of northern and southern Nigeria?
o: Northern Nigeria has a smaller daily temperature range but a larger annual range than the south
Northern Nigeria has a larger daily and annual temperature range than the south because it is farther from the moderating influence of the sea
Southern Nigeria has a larger annual temperature range because of its nearness to the sea
Both regions have identical daily and annual temperature ranges throughout the year
questions.e: Being farther inland and away from the sea's moderating effect, northern Nigeria experiences hotter days, cooler nights, and greater seasonal temperature swings than the humid south. The south, being closer to the ocean, has a more uniform temperature pattern with a smaller range.
questions.p: Because north Nigeria dey far from sea, dem dey experience hot days, cold nights, and bigger temperature range than south. South nearer to ocean, so dem temperature dey more uniform.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of rivers drains the Chad Basin of north-eastern Nigeria into Lake Chad?
o: River Hadejia and River Komadugu Yobe
questions.e: The Chad Basin in the north-east is drained by the Hadejia and Komadugu Yobe river system, which flows into Lake Chad. The other rivers listed belong to the Niger and Sokoto-Rima drainage systems in other parts of Nigeria.
questions.p: Na River Hadejia and Komadugu Yobe dey drain water go inside Lake Chad for north-east. Other rivers wey dem list dey flow go different places like Niger or Sokoto-Rima basin.

questions.q: A particular relief region of Nigeria is described as an undulating lowland lying mostly below 150 metres above sea level, bordering the Atlantic Ocean, and made up of recent sedimentary deposits with creeks, lagoons and sand bars. Which relief region is being described?
o: The coastal plains and Niger Delta
questions.e: The coastal plains and Niger Delta region is low-lying, below 150 metres, and consists of young sedimentary materials with lagoons, creeks and sand bars along the Atlantic coast. The Jos Plateau and Udi-Nsukka highlands are elevated areas, not low coastal lands.
questions.p: Dis place na coastal plains and Niger Delta because e low well well and get plenty sand bars and creeks. Jos Plateau and Udi-Nsukka highlands na high ground, no be low land.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the Sudan savanna vegetation of northern Nigeria consists mainly of short scattered trees and grasses, unlike the tall forest of the south?
o: Lower and more seasonal rainfall in the north limits tree growth and favours drought-resistant grasses
Northern Nigeria lies closer to the equator than southern Nigeria
The northern soils are naturally more fertile than southern soils, favouring grass over trees
Harmattan winds in the north increase soil moisture, which favours grasses over trees
questions.e: Rainfall in the north is lower in total amount and concentrated in a shorter wet season, so only drought-resistant grasses and scattered short trees can survive. Northern Nigeria is actually farther from the equator than the south, and harmattan dries rather than moistens the soil.
questions.p: Rain no too fall for north and the time wey rain dey fall short, so na only grass and small trees fit survive. Harmattan dey dry ground, e no dey give moisture.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relief of the Niger-Benue trough?
o: It is the highest relief region in Nigeria, exceeding 2,000 metres above sea level
It is located entirely along the Atlantic coastline of Nigeria
It is a broad lowland formed along the valleys of the River Niger and River Benue, lying generally below 300 metres
It consists mainly of ancient crystalline rocks forming steep-sided plateaus
questions.e: The Niger-Benue trough is a lowland region formed by the valleys of the two major rivers, generally lying below 300 metres above sea level. It is not Nigeria's highest region, is not made of ancient crystalline plateau rocks, and does not lie along the coast.
questions.p: Niger-Benue trough na big lowland wey dey below 300 metres. E no be high mountain and e no dey for coast.

questions.q: A particular Nigerian climate station records a mean annual rainfall of about 1,900 mm spread over eight to nine months, a mean annual temperature of around 26°C, and almost no distinct dry season of the harsh harmattan type. Which climatic type is most likely being described, and in which part of Nigeria is it typically found?
o: Semi-arid type, found around the Chad Basin in the north-east
Highland type, found on the Jos Plateau
Tropical continental type, found in the far north around Sokoto and Katsina
Tropical monsoon type, found in the extreme south-east around the Niger Delta and Calabar area
questions.e: High rainfall above 1,800 mm, a long wet season of eight to nine months and the near absence of a harsh dry season point to the tropical monsoon climate found in the extreme south-east, such as around Calabar and the Niger Delta. The continental and semi-arid types of the north have much lower rainfall and a long harmattan period, while the Jos Plateau has a cooler highland climate.
questions.p: Plenty rain and long wet season wey no get harsh harmattan na sign of tropical monsoon climate for south-east. North get dry weather and harmattan, while Jos Plateau get cool highland weather.

questions.q: Nigeria's location roughly between the Sahara Desert to the north and the Atlantic Ocean to the south has which of the following major effects on its climate?
o: It makes southern Nigeria drier than northern Nigeria
It prevents moist winds from the Atlantic Ocean from reaching any part of Nigeria
It produces a gradual transition from humid equatorial conditions in the south to drier tropical continental conditions in the north
It causes the whole country to experience uniform desert conditions throughout the year
questions.e: Because Nigeria stretches from the Atlantic coast to the edge of the Sahara, moisture-bearing winds from the ocean influence the south more than the north, creating a climatic gradient from wet equatorial conditions in the south to drier continental conditions in the north. The other options wrongly describe Nigeria as uniformly desert or reverse the actual rainfall pattern.
questions.p: Because Nigeria dey between Sahara desert and Atlantic Ocean, weather dey change from wet for south go dry for north. The ocean wind dey make south wet, while north dey dry.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the general direction of flow of the River Niger from its source to the point where it enters Nigeria, before it curves southward towards the sea?
o: It rises in Cameroon and flows westward into Nigeria through the Benue trough
It rises in the Fouta Djallon highlands of Guinea and flows north-east then curves south-east through Mali and Niger Republic into Nigeria
It rises on the Jos Plateau and flows directly south into the Atlantic Ocean
It rises in Lake Chad and flows westward across northern Nigeria
questions.e: The River Niger rises in the Fouta Djallon highlands of Guinea, flows north-eastward in a great bend through Mali and Niger Republic, and then curves south-eastward into Nigeria before draining into the Atlantic Ocean through the Niger Delta. It does not rise on the Jos Plateau, Lake Chad, or in Cameroon, which is instead the source area of the River Benue.
questions.p: River Niger start from Fouta Djallon for Guinea, e flow go north-east before e turn go south-east enter Nigeria. E no start for Jos Plateau or Lake Chad.

questions.q: A major factor that encourages groundnut cultivation as a cash crop in parts of Northern Nigeria, particularly around Kano and Katsina, is best described as
o: light sandy soils combined with a distinct dry season suitable for the crop
swampy, waterlogged lowlands ideal for groundnut root development
heavy annual rainfall exceeding 2000 mm supporting continuous cropping
dense tropical rainforest providing shade for young groundnut plants
questions.e: Groundnut thrives in light, well-drained sandy soils and requires a marked dry season for the pods to mature and be harvested easily. These conditions are typical of the Sudan and Sahel savanna areas of Kano and Katsina, unlike rainforest or swampy environments.
questions.p: Groundnut dey grow well for sandy soil wey water no dey stay too much. E also need dry season make di pods dry well before dem harvest am, na why Kano and Katsina dey good for am.

questions.q: The iron and steel industry at Ajaokuta was sited mainly because of its relative nearness to which combination of resource needs for steel production?
o: Large groundnut farms supplying raw material and labour
Cocoa plantations and a nearby international airport
Crude oil deposits and a deep seaport for export
Iron ore from Itakpe and coal/limestone sources plus River Niger for water and transport
questions.e: Ajaokuta was chosen because it lies close to Itakpe iron ore deposits and sources of coal and limestone needed as raw materials, while the River Niger supplies water for industrial processes and aids transportation. Crude oil, groundnuts and cocoa are not the key inputs for iron and steel production.
questions.p: Dem put Ajaokuta for dat side because e near Itakpe iron ore and coal. River Niger also dey help dem carry water and transport heavy things for di factory.

questions.q: Nigeria's tin and columbite mining activities are most closely associated with which physical region of the country?
questions.e: Tin and columbite mining in Nigeria developed mainly on the Jos Plateau, where these minerals occur in alluvial and primary deposits within the basement complex rocks. The other regions listed are not known for these specific minerals.
questions.p: Na Jos Plateau dem dey see plenty tin and columbite for Nigeria. Na inside di rocks for dat area dem dey find dis minerals.

questions.q: A geography student observes that a particular Nigerian industry depends heavily on imported raw materials, is concentrated in Lagos and Port Harcourt because of good port facilities, and its finished products are mostly re-exported or distributed nationwide by road. This description most likely refers to which type of industry?
o: Assembly-type industry such as vehicle or electronics assembly
Subsistence fishing industry along the coast
Agro-based processing industry using local cocoa
questions.e: Assembly-type industries, such as vehicle or electronics assembly plants, typically rely on imported components, locate near ports for easy importation, and distribute finished goods nationwide by road. Agro-based, craft and fishing industries do not fit this pattern of heavy import dependence and port-based siting.
questions.p: Assembly industries like car or electronics dey depend on parts wey dem dey import from abroad. Dem dey stay near port so dat e go easy to bring di parts enter and carry finish product go round di country.

questions.q: In terms of Nigeria's population structure, a geography textbook describes the country's population pyramid as having a very broad base that narrows rapidly towards the top. This shape best indicates that Nigeria has
o: equal numbers of people in every age group
a declining population due to low birth rates
a high birth rate and high dependency ratio with a youthful population
an ageing population with more elderly than young people
questions.e: A broad base on a population pyramid shows a large number of children, which reflects a high birth rate, while the narrowing top shows fewer older people due to a shorter life expectancy. This pattern is typical of developing countries like Nigeria with youthful, fast-growing populations and high dependency ratios.
questions.p: Di broad base for di pyramid show say plenty pikin dey born every year. Because di top narrow, e mean say people no dey live reach old age too much, so di young ones plenty pass.

questions.q: A farming community in the Niger Delta practises fishing and oil palm processing side by side, but a government survey shows that oil exploration activities have polluted several creeks, reducing fish catch by 40% over five years while palm oil output remained steady. Which of the following best explains why palm oil production was less affected than fishing in this scenario?
o: Palm oil processing requires no water at any stage of production
Oil palm trees grow on land away from the polluted waterways, unlike fish which live directly in the creeks
Fishing communities abandoned their trade voluntarily due to low market prices
Government banned fishing but encouraged palm oil processing instead
questions.e: Because oil palm trees are cultivated on land, pollution of creeks and rivers from oil spillage has a limited direct effect on them compared to fish, which live in the water and are directly exposed to contaminants. This explains why fish catch dropped sharply while palm oil output stayed stable, not because of policy bans or market abandonment.
questions.p: Oil palm tree dey grow for land, so oil wey spill for water no go affect am like fish. Fish dey live inside di water, so once di water dirty, di fish go die or run comot.

questions.q: The 2006 National Population Census figures showed that Kano State had one of the highest population counts among Nigerian states. Which of the following factors best explains this high population concentration?
o: Presence of extensive crude oil deposits attracting migrant workers
Long history of urban settlement, trade and favourable agricultural land supporting dense rural population
Location along the coast encouraging fishing settlements
Heavy rainfall throughout the year favouring rice cultivation
questions.e: Kano's long history as a centre of trade, Islamic scholarship and agriculture on fertile savanna land has supported dense settlement for centuries. It has no oil deposits, heavy year-round rainfall, or coastal location.
questions.p: Kano don tey as big center for business, Islam learning, and agriculture inside good land, na im make plenty people dey stay there. E no get crude oil or heavy rain every time like coastal places.

questions.q: A geography teacher tells her class that Nigeria's population growth rate remains high mainly because of a combination of a particular birth rate pattern and a changing death rate pattern. Which combination correctly describes this situation?
o: Low birth rate and rising death rate due to disease outbreaks
High birth rate and high death rate, keeping growth low
Low birth rate and low death rate, keeping growth stable
High birth rate and declining death rate due to improved health care
questions.e: Nigeria still has a high birth rate while improved health care and sanitation have reduced the death rate. This combination produces rapid natural population increase.
questions.p: Nigeria still dey born plenty children well well, but better health care and clean environment don make people stop to die anyhow. Dis one dey make the population population grow fast fast.

questions.q: A cooperative society in Benue State wants to set up a cassava processing plant. An agricultural extension officer advises that this crop is a major staple widely cultivated across the Middle Belt mainly because of which condition?
o: Very high altitude with cool temperatures suited only to temperate crops
Extremely low rainfall requiring irrigation for any crop to survive
Moderate rainfall, fairly fertile loamy soils and a long growing season suited to root crops
Continuous flooding throughout the year suited only to rice
questions.e: The Middle Belt has moderate rainfall and fertile loamy soils with a long growing season, which favours root crops like cassava and yam. The other conditions described do not match the Middle Belt's actual climate.
questions.p: Middle Belt get moderate rainfall and good soil wey dey stay long time for ground crop like cassava and yam. Other options no talk true about how Middle Belt weather be.

questions.q: A mining company surveys an area and finds commercially viable deposits of bitumen close to the surface. Based on known Nigerian mineral distribution, in which part of the country is this survey most likely taking place?
o: Ondo State area in the South-West
Borno State area in the North-East
Taraba State area in the North-East
Sokoto State area in the far North-West
questions.e: Nigeria's major bitumen deposits occur in Ondo State and parts of the South-West, forming one of the world's largest bitumen belts. The other states are not known for significant bitumen deposits.
questions.p: Na Ondo State and other South-West places dem dey see plenty bitumen for Nigeria. The other states wey dem mention no get this kind mineral at all.

questions.q: An industrial geographer compares two Nigerian manufacturing industries: one processes groundnuts into oil near Kano, while another assembles imported vehicle parts near Lagos. What is the key difference in locational factor between these two industries?
o: The groundnut oil industry is market-oriented while the vehicle assembly industry is raw-material-oriented
The groundnut oil industry is raw-material-oriented while the vehicle assembly industry depends on port access for imported components
Both industries depend entirely on nearness to coal deposits
Both industries are located mainly because of nearness to hydro-electric power stations
questions.e: Groundnut oil milling is sited near Kano because it processes bulky local raw materials grown nearby, reducing transport cost of the raw crop. Vehicle assembly near Lagos depends on easy port access for importing component parts, a different locational logic entirely.
questions.p: Groundnut oil factory near Kano because of raw material wey dey close, so transport go cheap. But car assembly near Lagos na because of sea port to bring in motor part from outside.

questions.q: A rural community in Kebbi State practises irrigation farming along the Sokoto-Rima river floodplain, producing onions and wheat mainly in the dry season. This farming method is best described as which of the following?
questions.e: Fadama farming uses the fertile floodplains of rivers for dry-season irrigation farming, common along the Sokoto-Rima valley for crops like onions and wheat. Shifting cultivation and bush fallowing are rain-fed rotational systems, not irrigation-based.
questions.p: Fadama farming na when people use river flood land to plant during dry season for Sokoto-Rima valley. Shifting cultivation and bush fallowing na rain-fed system, no be irrigation.

questions.q: A planning officer compares two Nigerian towns: Town P has a population of 450,000 people spread over 900 square kilometres, while Town Q has a population of 800,000 people spread over 400 square kilometres. By how many persons per square kilometre is the population density of Town Q greater than that of Town P?
questions.e: Town P's density is 450,000 divided by 900, which equals 500 persons per square kilometre. Town Q's density is 800,000 divided by 400, which equals 2,000 persons per square kilometre, so the difference is 2,000 minus 500 equals 1,500.
questions.p: Town P density na 500 persons per square kilometre, while Town Q density na 2,000 persons per square kilometre. When you minus 500 from 2,000, you go get 1,500 difference.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of Nigerian cities is directly linked by a railway line that forms part of the original narrow-gauge network built during the colonial era?
questions.e: The Lagos to Kano railway line was one of the earliest major colonial railway routes built to move agricultural produce and minerals to the coast for export. It remains a key reference route in Nigeria's rail network.
questions.p: Na Lagos to Kano railway line dem build early for colonial time to carry farm produce and minerals go coast. E still dey important inside Nigeria rail network today.

questions.q: A major reason why air transport, despite being the fastest means of transport in Nigeria, carries the smallest proportion of total passenger and freight traffic is that it
o: is banned from carrying agricultural produce across state boundaries
cannot operate during the rainy season because of persistent cloud cover
requires very high fares and costly infrastructure that most Nigerians cannot easily afford
depends entirely on imported aircraft that are unavailable in Nigeria
questions.e: Air transport involves expensive aircraft, fuel, airport facilities and maintenance, so fares are high compared to other means. This limits the number of people and amount of goods that can use it, unlike road or rail transport.
questions.p: Aircraft work with expensive machine, fuel and maintenance, so ticket price high pass other transport. Naim make many people and goods no dey use am like road or train.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the main attraction of the Obudu Mountain Resort in Cross River State to tourists?
o: Its location as the site of Nigeria's largest annual trade fair
Its position as the deepest natural harbour along the Nigerian coast
Its status as the terminus of the eastern railway line to the coast
Its cool highland climate, scenic ranch landscape and cable car ride
questions.e: Obudu Mountain Resort is popular mainly because of its cool temperate-like climate at high altitude, cattle ranch scenery and the cable car that carries visitors up the escarpment. It is not known for trade fairs, harbours or railways.
questions.p: Obudu Mountain Resort sweet people because of cold weather, fine cattle ranch, and cable car wey dey carry visitors up. E no be place for trade fair, ship harbour, or train.

questions.q: Nigeria's export trade is described as largely dominated by primary products because the country mainly sells
o: crude oil, cocoa and other raw agricultural and mineral products with little processing
manufactured machinery and refined petrochemical products to neighbouring countries
finished textiles and assembled vehicles produced in local factories
processed foods and pharmaceuticals manufactured for the West African market
questions.e: A large share of Nigeria's export earnings comes from crude oil and raw agricultural products such as cocoa, which are exported with little or no processing. This pattern is typical of countries whose trade is dominated by primary products.
questions.p: Plenty money wey Nigeria dey make from export na from crude oil and raw cocoa wey dem no process well. Dis one show say na primary products dey dominate trade.

questions.q: A transport planner observes that a particular pipeline network in Nigeria is specifically designed to move refined petroleum products such as petrol and kerosene from refineries to depots in different parts of the country, rather than crude oil to export terminals. This pipeline system is best classified as part of
o: the upstream crude oil export network
the downstream petroleum products distribution network
questions.e: Pipelines carrying refined products like petrol and kerosene from refineries to storage depots belong to the downstream sector, which deals with processing and distribution to final consumers. Crude oil movement to export terminals is instead part of the upstream sector.
questions.p: Pipeline wey dey carry refined fuel like petrol and kerosene from refinery go depot na downstream sector work. Crude oil movement go export port na upstream business.

questions.q: A trader in Kano imports electronic goods through the port of Cotonou in Benin Republic and then transports them overland into Nigeria without the goods passing through any formal Nigerian customs clearance. This practice, which denies Nigeria useful trade revenue, is best described as
questions.e: Bringing goods into a country through unofficial routes to avoid customs duties and clearance is known as smuggling. It differs from entrepot trade, which involves officially importing goods for the purpose of legally re-exporting them.
questions.p: To bring goods enter country through back door to avoid customs duty na smuggling. E different from entrepot trade where person legally import goods to re-export dem.

questions.q: Along a certain stretch of the Niger River used for inland water transport, a hydrographic survey recorded the river depth at five points during the dry season as 1.2 metres, 0.9 metres, 1.5 metres, 0.8 metres and 1.1 metres. If a cargo barge requires a minimum depth of 1.3 metres to move safely without grounding, what is the average depth recorded along this stretch, and can the barge safely use the entire stretch during this period?
o: Average depth is 0.9 metres, so the barge can safely use the entire stretch
Average depth is 1.3 metres, so the barge can safely use the entire stretch
Average depth is 1.1 metres, so the barge cannot safely use the entire stretch
Average depth is 1.5 metres, so the barge can safely use the entire stretch
questions.e: Adding the five depths gives 5.5 metres, and dividing by 5 gives an average of 1.1 metres, which is below the required 1.3 metres. Also, three of the five points measured are shallower than 1.3 metres, so the barge would ground at those points and cannot safely use the whole stretch.
questions.p: If you add all five depths and divide by five, you go get 1.1 metres, which dey below the 1.3 metres wey the barge need. Dat mean the barge no fit use the river stretch safely.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major tourist attraction found in Yankari Game Reserve in Bauchi State?
questions.e: Wikki Warm Spring is the well-known natural spring found inside Yankari Game Reserve in Bauchi State. The other features are located in different states of Nigeria.
questions.p: Na Wikki Warm Spring dey inside Yankari Game Reserve for Bauchi State. Di other places dey different states for Nigeria.

questions.q: One major reason why Nigeria's internal trade in foodstuffs is seasonal in nature is that
o: most food crops are harvested at specific times of the year due to the rainfall pattern
foodstuffs are mainly produced for export rather than local consumption
government policy bans the sale of food crops all year round
traders prefer to sell manufactured goods instead of food crops
questions.e: Nigeria has distinct wet and dry seasons, so food crops are planted and harvested at particular times, making their supply and trade seasonal. This is why prices of foodstuffs often rise sharply in the off-season.
questions.p: Nigeria get wet and dry season, so dem dey harvest food crops for specific time of the year. E make the trade and supply of food sake of season.

questions.q: A commodity market in which farmers and traders from different villages gather on specific fixed days, such as every fifth day, to buy and sell goods is best described as a
questions.e: A periodic market operates on fixed recurring days rather than every day, which is common in rural parts of Nigeria where demand does not justify a daily market. Daily and terminal markets operate continuously or serve as final distribution points regardless of a fixed cycle.
questions.p: Periodic market dey happen for fixed days instead of everyday. Naim make people from villages dey gather sell and buy goods on top specific days.

questions.q: ECOWAS was established with the main aim of promoting cooperation among member states chiefly in which area?
o: Control of the United Nations Security Council
Economic integration and trade among member states
questions.e: ECOWAS was formed mainly to promote economic cooperation, trade and development among West African states. The other options are unrelated to its founding purpose.
questions.p: ECOWAS dem form am mainly to make West African countries dey work together for trade and money matter. No be for war or religion dem take start the group.

questions.q: West Africa's vegetation belts change from south to north mainly in response to a decrease in rainfall. Which sequence correctly shows this change from the coast towards the Sahara?
o: Mangrove swamp, rainforest, guinea savanna, sudan savanna, sahel savanna
Sahel savanna, sudan savanna, guinea savanna, rainforest, mangrove swamp
Rainforest, sahel savanna, guinea savanna, mangrove swamp, sudan savanna
Guinea savanna, rainforest, mangrove swamp, sudan savanna, sahel savanna
questions.e: Moving from the coast northward, rainfall reduces steadily, producing this correct order of vegetation belts. The other options wrongly reverse or mix up the sequence.
questions.p: As you dey comot from sea side dey go north, rain dey reduce, so the plants dey change small small. Na this order show how the vegetation dey follow rain pattern.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major economic activity that most ECOWAS member states depend on, making regional trade policies on cash crops like cocoa, groundnut and cotton very important?
o: Agriculture and export of primary commodities
questions.e: Most West African economies rely heavily on agriculture, especially cash crop production and export. The other options do not reflect the dominant economic activities of the region.
questions.p: Plenty West African countries dey depend on farming to survive. Na why cocoa and groundnut matter dey very important for our trade policy.

questions.q: A new ECOWAS trade protocol removes import duties on goods that are wholly produced within member states, such as cocoa from Ghana sold in Nigeria. This protocol is best described as promoting which of the following?
o: A political federation of West Africa
A free trade area among member states
questions.e: Removing tariffs on goods produced within the community creates a free trade area, which is a core economic integration tool of ECOWAS. The other options describe political or cultural arrangements, not trade.
questions.p: If country no collect tax for goods wey dem produce inside the region, e mean say dem don create free trade area. This one na way to make business flow well between members.

questions.q: Lake Chad, an important water resource shared by several West and Central African countries, has been reported to be shrinking over recent decades. Which of these is the most likely consequence for ECOWAS countries bordering it?
o: Increased conflict over fishing and grazing land as water resources reduce
Rapid rise in sea level along the Atlantic coast
Automatic expansion of farmland due to more rainfall
Permanent increase in fish stock available to fishermen
questions.e: As Lake Chad shrinks, competition over the remaining water, fishing grounds and grazing land increases tension among communities and countries. The other options describe the opposite of what shrinking water bodies cause.
questions.p: As Lake Chad dey dry finish, water and land wey people dey use for farm and fish dey reduce. This one dey cause wahala and fight between the people wey dey live there.

questions.q: An ECOWAS trade analyst notes that Niger, being landlocked, relies on a coastal member state's port and road network to export its goods to Europe. Which country's ports would most logically serve this purpose, based on shared border and existing transport routes?
questions.e: Benin shares a border with Niger and has a well-used port-to-Niger transport corridor through Cotonou. Senegal, Cape Verde and Sierra Leone are too far or not directly connected by land routes to Niger.
questions.p: Niger no get sea, so dem dey use Benin port to carry their goods go outside. Benin dey close to Niger and the road dey connect well.

questions.q: A geography teacher explains that despite ECOWAS's integration efforts, trade among member states remains relatively low compared to trade with countries outside the region. Which factor best explains this situation?
o: Member states have identical colonial languages, removing all trade barriers
Member states mostly produce similar primary products, reducing the need to trade with each other
ECOWAS has banned all cross-border trade between member states
All member states use the same currency, eliminating exchange rate problems
questions.e: Many West African countries produce similar raw materials and cash crops, so there is little complementary demand for each other's goods, pushing them to trade more with industrialised regions outside West Africa. The other options are factually incorrect about ECOWAS.
questions.p: Most countries for West Africa dey produce the same kind of raw materials. Because everybody dey produce the same thing, e dey hard to trade with each other.
